chapters.title: Chapter 1: Just Another PR Stunt
chapters.html:
“I’m sorry, what?”

Phainon asked again, with a sharper voice and a higher pitch. He did not actually miss what the man next to him had said. He heard it just fine the first time. He just wanted him to repeat it, just to be sure that he got it right.

On the passenger seat, Mydei, the love of his life, the man who had met his parents on barbecue night a few weekends back in Phainon’s hometown, the man who inspired the matching ring he commissioned Cartonus, the famous rockstar with ten million followers on Chrystagram, pressed his lips and sighed in that particular way that told Phainon that he would rather fight a man twice his size than have to repeat it. But Phainon pretended he overlooked that.

Reality was cruel, Mydeimos, he whispered in his own mind. You have to face it. You’re not an exception to its cruelty just because you’re pretty.

“I said,” Mydei said, slower this time, with every drag of his words conveying his dismay. “They want me to have this fake relationship with that pop star Clockie Princess girl.”

Ah.

So Phainon really got it right the first time.

He kind of lowkey hoped he had mistaken it for something else, for some reason. Like, maybe he had turned deaf with how many times he flies to the sky. Perhaps his driving skills had dulled to the point that he could no longer have a proper conversation while he had one foot on the gas.

“Is that so.”

“Hm.”

“They want you to have a fake relationship with Robin.”

“That’s what I just said.”

“The Popstar Robin.”

“Yes.”

“The super famous child actress, super talented singer, everybody’s sweetheart Robin.”

“HKS!”

Phainon couldn’t help but let out a little snicker at Mydei’s malicious hiss. He glanced at the beautiful man from his peripheral vision, only to be welcomed with the deepest furrow of the other’s brows. His thin lips pressed tight in distaste, and boy, did this muscular man with a black outfit from head to toe, red tattoo to complete his rebellious look, and fiery golden eyes look adorable when he sulked.

Phainon almost wanted to pull over just to kiss him.

But he was very proud of his impeccable self-control, so Phainon cleared his throat and pushed that thought aside. “Sorry, ‘Dei, just had to be sure,” he said. “I just don’t get it. Why Robin, all of a sudden, among all the celebrities and people and Halovians in the world, choose to approach you now?”

“Beat me.”

Phainon punched Mydei’s arm. Mydei returned it with twice the vigor.

Ah, he loves this man.

“Hmm, let me think, maybe she’s dating someone worse, and you’re being used as a distraction,” Phainon hummed. “Or maybe she’s gay? Oh, oh! Maybe she’s pregnant, and they decided that a hot, badass man who says let’s rock the fucking world on public television is a perfect scapegoat to be framed as the irresponsible Dad who ditches the kid.”

Mydei rolled his eyes. “Stop watching that Gardishians Show, Phainon. Your brain starts to rot,” he hissed in pure annoyance, and Phainon couldn’t help but let out a wheezing laugh.

“Hey, don’t trash them like that! Hyacine actually liked them. Well, in a way that she wants to cure their issues,” he said. When Mydei did not let up the glare, Phainon raised his fingers from the steering wheel. “Okay, sorry, sorry. Back to the topic. You still did not answer the why?”

Mydei groaned, wiping his face with his hands as he stared out of the window, looking so hard to convey how miserable he felt. “The heck I know why. Aglaea only told me that part. She said they will fill me in when I arrive,” he said—still sulking, still adorable.

Phainon began to question the impeccable self-control he had been so proud of a moment earlier.

“Ooooh, the mystery.”

Mydei punched Phainon’s arm. Thrice the power.

“Ow!”  Phainon said. It didn’t actually hurt. He just wanted to mess with Mydei. “Wait, they?”

“Yeah. Aglaea said she will be there too,” Mydei said gruffly.

“Who, Robin?”

“No, the janitor. Yes, Robin, Phainon. Who do you think?” Mydei barked.

Phainon couldn’t help but burst into laughter. “Damn, you’re awfully pissy since you took that call, man,” he said. “Wait, is that why you insist on dragging me along? Because you want me to meet Robin? Aww, my sweet Pomme Honeycake, how thoughtful of you. You know how much of a Robin fan I am.”

From his peripheral vision, Phainon could see Mydei completely zeroed in on Phainon, ignoring his jokes and looking straight up, baffled, like he was questioning his life choices, including why he was dating a dumbass like Phainon. It looked cute, still. But also dangerous, like Mydei was on the verge of turning into Nikador himself and impaling Phainon with his Lance of Fury.

“What?” Phainon demanded, feeling nervous now.

“You can’t be this dumb, HKS,” he said. “That’s not why I want you there at all!”

“Oh, uh, so you just want me to drive you there because you don’t want to lose a moment of our precious weekend together? That’s romantic too!”

Mydei sighed. Yes, that definitely looked like he was questioning his life choices.

“HKS! Don’t you get even slightly disturbed that I will be having a public relationship with someone else?”

This time, Mydei sounded so damn serious that Phainon’s teasing smile faltered. He paused and glanced at Mydei, who was still staring at him like a cat with its claws out, ready to strike if he did not like what Phainon would say next.

“Um… that’s a fake relationship, right?”

“Yeah. But a relationship.”

“Yeah… but it’s not real, right? Like, an act?” Phainon paused. “I… uh, I think it’s fine, depending on the reason. And It’s Aglaea. She always has a good reason, so….”

Mydei raised his brows. “Huh,” he scoffed. “Almost looks like you’re fine with the idea of me being in a relationship with someone else.”

Okay, he definitely did not like Phainon’s answer at all.

“No, ‘Dei, c’mon, think about it, the whole idea is just so silly. I mean, you, Robin, a fake relationship. Come on, you’re famous, she’s even more famous. No one’s benefitting from this… arrangement whatsoever.

Someone’s just messing with you,” Phainon said. His smile did not falter, but his voice got a bit more serious now. Mydei seemed to believe that this was a real situation.

Maybe it was.

Maybe Phainon simply didn't understand the world of rock stars and celebrities. He never had to before this. Mydei was always kind enough to keep him out of that part of his life throughout their relationship.

So really, he didn’t know how he should behave now. It was new to him that Mydei was suddenly involving him in his decision about something in his career. Normally he limited that kind of interaction on music and lyrics alone, asking Phainon if it sounded good or if the lyrics sounded too cliche.

Mydei narrowed his eyes. “Aglaea messing with me?”

Phainon shrugged. Okay, now that sounds silly. “Yeah, that doesn’t make sense. I don’t know. Maybe it’s a prank? Perhaps your album or concert ticket reaches a certain milestone, and they want to celebrate with a surprise? Have you checked the news? The socials? Try asking Anaxa. He won’t lie about these kinds of things.”

Mydei scoffed. “No need,” he said. “We’ll be there soon enough. We’ll just have to hear what they want.”

Phainon nodded. Yeah, that sounded about right. He pulled up to the building he knew too well and grabbed the parking ticket. Only when the parking ticket was printed did it dawn on him.

“Wait, we?”

- Mydeimos, the main vocalist and frontman of the super-famous rock band Sons of Gorgo, the love of his life, the man Phainon would do anything for, dragged him along to the elevator that climbed to the high floor of the Mnestia Tower, not caring about the fact that three security layers eyed Phainon with disdain (probably more because he was holding hands with Mydeimos the rockstar, not because of his fashion sense).

Still, when Phainon saw his reflection on the elevator walls, he noticed his worn-out jeans, dirty sneakers, and a black shirt with a massive "I <3 OKHEMA" sign printed on the front. Even Phainon caught on to how messy he looked.

“You finally see what the rest of us feel when we look at how you dressed,” Mydei said, upon hearing Phainon’s groan and the horror in Phainon’s eyes.

“I did not know I was gonna be dragged along to enter the building! I thought you’d told me to wait in the car!” Phainon hissed. “If I’d known that you would do this, I wouldn’t have agreed to drive you in the first place. I don’t have a clean shirt. Yesterday was supposed to be my laundry day, and you kept me occupied the whole day.”

Phainon pressed an index finger to Mydei’s chest, only for him to let out a smug smirk.

This bastard. He’s super lucky that he’s cute.

“You’re coming along regardless, HKS,” Mydei said as he tightened his hold on their entwined fingers. He paused, staring at the climbing number above the elevator’s door as he continued. “I need you there.”

Mydei’s voice remained calm, but something was wavering on the edge of his voice; something that sounded like exhaustion, nervousness, anger… Phainon couldn’t quite catch what that was. But from the look of his golden eyes, Phainon could tell that Mydei was being serious, and so Phainon nodded.

It’s very rare for Mydei to admit out loud that he needed Phainon outside the bedroom. Mydei was usually very reserved and impossibly prideful when he was not high on libido. So Phainon wouldn’t betray him and be the best boyfriend he could be, just as he always promised Mydei.

The elevator door dinged, and the next thing Phainon knew, he entered a large, super opulent room made of mahogany, marble, and crystal chandeliers with gold accents all across. A room that screamed Aglaea in the first second he was there.

Inside that lavish room, a few people were chatting in hushed voices. The first person Phainon noticed was Aglaea behind her desk, with Anaxa, her husband, just next to her, raising his brows at Phainon in a way that said he was surprised by Phainon’s presence.

Then, on the sofa meant for guests, Phainon could see three figures sitting, glancing at the door as he and Mydeimos entered the room. On the single sofa, he saw a blond man in a flashy outfit and pink-tinted sunglasses, who shifted his gaze toward them, raising his brows upon noticing their presence. And on the loveseat sat a more stern, serious-looking guy with silver eyes, and… Robin.

The Robin.

Phainon had seen her hundreds and hundreds of times on TV, the big screen, and digital videos. He thought that he wouldn’t be surprised to see her in person. Yet, she could still somehow surprise him. Robin looked even more petite than Phainon had imagined. She was way, way more beautiful. The lighting, makeup, camera filters, and post-production alterations did not do her beauty justice at all.

She was a star on the screen. Now, in person, she looked like a literal angel.

Robin nodded with a small smile at Phainon and Mydei, greeting them with a wave and a small hello.

Phainon could swear that his heart stopped.

Before anyone could say anything else, before Mydei could even grunt in annoyance, the pink-sunglasses blond man rose from his seat, smiling as he opened his arms to greet Mydei.

“Well, hello, if it isn’t the Prince of rock himself,” he announced in an absolutely confident way, almost looking like he was trying to be seductive. The blond man was small, a few inches shorter than Phainon, but his presence quickly filled the room as he approached Mydei. “Look at you, looking far more handsome and sturdier up close.”

The man patted Mydei’s biceps playfully, to which Mydei quickly pulled away, and Phainon instinctively leaned to swat his hand. The man flashed a bright smile as he glanced at Phainon. He still looked confident and relaxed, but wow, his eyes…

How could Phainon feel so little under the gaze of a man shorter than him?

“I’m sorry, is….Okhema supposed to be here?” he said, giving Phainon half a once-over before he apparently decided that Phainon was not worth his time. “I thought I made it clear when I said that this is a private meeting. No guards or assistants allowed.”

“Oh, my name is Pha…”, “He’s staying,” “Cut to the chase, Aventurine.”

The man smiled even more smugly in front of Phainon, Mydeimos, and Aglaea’s words.

“Alright, wow,” he said, flashing a wink at Mydei as he continued. “Whatever. So you’ve heard of my brilliant plan, yes, Mydeimos? Have you decided to agree with it yet? Trust me, it’s going to happen in a very short timeline. In just six months, you will collaborate with Robin; she will join you on the upcoming summer tour; you two will act lovey-dovey on stage; and maybe have a few lunches and dates here and there. Nothing too giving. Fans would eat it up more if you only gave them hints to fantasize about. It will be over before you know—”

“Yeah, before all of that, get to the why,” Mydei cut the man’s words.

The man—(Aventurine, as Aglaea called him) paused, staring at Mydei in a mild, visible surprise that made Phainon sure that no one had ever cut his words so brashly like that before. His smile remained, but the purple in his eyes sparkled in a way that Phainon could describe as murder intent.

Okay, this tiny guy was clearly not someone you could mess with. He looked like someone who would orchestrate a whole social media campaign to annihilate your character if you did as much as getting into his bad side.

Phainon subconsciously straightened up, brushing his thumb on Mydei’s hand.

“Ahem, Mister Aventurine, please allow me,” Robin got up from her seat. Her voice was smooth, her smile was gentle, and as she stood, Phainon could see her white, airy dress flutter like a gentle feather that made a swan beautiful. That dress made even getting up from a seat look like a graceful awakening for her.

Phainon bit the inner of his lower lip. The sharp turn from Aventurine’s dangerous aura to Robin’s gentle, calming presence was so quick that he almost felt his head spinning.

Robin nodded at Aventurine, her smile a sign of gratitude and… reassurance. Huh. She probably had realized the shift in Aventurine’s mood, too, and perhaps decided that it would be easier for the conversation to progress if she just jumped in.

Beautiful and smart, too.

Is she even real?

“Hello, Mydeimos. First of all, my name is Robin. And I’m so happy I can finally meet you in person. I’m a huge fan of your art.”

Mydei nodded. He did not look like he was impressed with Robin at all, but Phainon could see that his edges were softening, if only for a little. His jaw was unclenched, but his glare was still there, hanging on out of habit.

“I know you,” Mydei said. “And so does the entire world and their mother. I guess you’ll be the person who will answer the why?”

The man beside Robin (his brother?) also got up from his seat, narrowing his eyes on Mydei like he was offended by the way Mydei treated his little sister. Robin instinctively held her brother’s wrist; her movement was so in sync that it was like she’d seen it coming.

“Yes,” she said. Her smile did not falter. “I am grateful that you and Miss Aglaea are willing to lend us an ear, despite this request being sprung on you all of a sudden. As you may have already heard, it is, at its core, nothing more than a humble request for a collaboration. As you may already know, I’m always a fan of Sons of Gorgo. Your music always makes me feel energetic when I’m feeling super down. I am a longtime fan, and I always look forward to a chance to collaborate with you or simply to attend your concert. But time never seems to allow me.”

She slipped a hair behind her ear, looking like a bashful fan at Mydei’s meet and greet. But like, a hundred times more graceful.

Phainon knew that she was not doing it for show. He once read an article about Robin in a Penacony Air in-flight magazine that revealed Robin’s top 10 playlist, and Mydei’s Regrets Are None was among the top three. Phainon remembered that he took a picture of it and shared it with Mydei, only for Mydei to respond with a thumbs-up emoji. So Mydei must have known that she was saying the truth, too.

“But a couple of weeks ago, my grandfather sent me a few vinyls that belonged to our dear mother, and I came across the vinyl from Queen Gorgo.”

She paused, as if waiting for Mydei’s reaction.

Again, good call.

Because Phainon could see that Mydei was stiffening, his grip on Phainon’s hand was even tighter now as she mentioned Mydei’s late mother's stage name. He was always like that; even though by far the mention of Queen Gorgo had always been followed by a positive commentary on her music and her image as the Undethroned Queen of Rock and Roll, Mydei always looked like he was bracing himself as if he were set to defend her against anything.

It was adorable, really—Mother’s most formidable defender, Mydeimos. Phainon wanted to kiss his cheek.

“I love your music, but hers was absolutely phenomenal, and I love, love, LOVE them so much! It was far ahead of its time; the surprising blend of blues and rock really reached the very core of my heart. I couldn’t stop listening to it, and I couldn’t stop thinking about it. Her music was so beautiful that it inspired me.”

Robin paused again, pressing her lips and blinking a few times, like she was trying not to fangirl. It was almost cute. Phainon almost wanted to coo.

How could someone be so beautiful, graceful, and adorably cute at the same time? What is she, really?

“I see,” Mydei scoffed. “Thank you on her behalf, I guess.”

“No, thank you, I’m so happy to even have the chance to appropriately express my praises. Your Mother is just amazing. I see where you get the talent and the inspiration from,” she smiled—a pristine image of Dollywood Royalty.

Phainon could feel Mydei tensing. Again.

“... and actually, this is why we’re here. I wrote a few songs as a tribute to her, and by some miracle, the Studios agreed to release them as my new summer release. But I think it is wrong to release them without involving you. Because you’re her son, and um… you’re the one who carries her legacy. So I think the proper way to release the songs is to involve you in a proper collaboration.”

Mydei shrugged. “If that’s the only reason, then just release them. No need to involve me,” Mydei said. “Musicians inspire each other all the time. I won’t sue you just because some of the beats you wrote sound similar to my Mom’s. I can name at least five underground bands that have done that. Why all the fuss of orchestrating the whole fake relationship thing?”

“Now, we finally get to the real problem,” the blond man with tacky fashion interrupted. Apparently, he had already given up his murderous intent and returned to that slimy smile attitude. “You see, Mydeimos. Robin can’t just do that. She can’t just walk out the door with heavy eyeliner and a black leather jacket and scream at the world. Robin has this brand about a girl next door. She’s our angel. Our sweet girl. She’s literally The Clockie Princess, you know that, right?”

The whole world knows that. But sure, by Kephale, forbid an artist from expressing himself, Phainon murmured in his head. But Mydei did not seem to be fazed.

“Yeah, and?”

“It means that she can’t just release a gritty, rebellious song with too many drums and screechy guitars on her own. It’s far too risky. Not just for her career, but for her image in general. I have a five-year-old daughter who sang Robin’s songs in class with her whole friend group, and those kids have matching keychains of Robin’s origami bird figure. We can’t just release rock-and-roll tracks all of a sudden. Not after the huge success of Inside. A sudden change of a pop star’s brand image was one of the top reasons for their fallout. The shock will literally kill the fans. So no, we can’t just release them without a care. It would be catastrophic.”

Translation: this guy didn’t want to lose sales on kids' merchandise once Robin is releasing a rock album. He didn’t want Robin to lose her popularity, which might cost him half of his enormous paycheck.

Yeah, catastrophic indeed.

“So don’t release it, then,” Mydei said, looking all baffled now, like he didn’t even understand why they were having this conversation at all.

Which Phainon agreed wholeheartedly. If it was going to have such a huge risk for her image, then why bother releasing those songs?

“I can answer why that would be such a huge loss, Mydei, and I don’t even talk about profit,” Anaxa chimed in from his place next to Aglaea. “Ratio had sent me a few samples of the tracks, and they’re bangers. It was far too cool, definitely far too amazing to be left dusty in the corner.”

Now, since it’s Anaxa, Phainon knew that it must come from a place of professionalism—an absolute truth. Anaxa loved Queen Gorgo. He still is, hence why he was very insistent that Mydei join his label when Sons of Gorgo was first formed. And Phainon was not very familiar with the music industry, but he was aware of Dr. Ratio. He was a genius producer who had worked with famous stars such as The Trailblazers, Boothill, and Lynx and The Landaus.

“I think we should listen to the samples now,” Aglaea added. “So it would be fair for Mydei.”

The room waited, and Mydei only shrugged. “Sure,” he said. “Go ahead.”

Aglaea typed on her laptop, and then a rhythmic guitar riff came through, followed by punchy drums and piano chords from the sound system in her room.

Then, a raw, gritty, commanding woman‘s voice was heard, singing with the air of smoky confidence. The snarl, the sharp yeah, the raspy verses were so sharp, so confident, like it was sung from the peak of Queen Gorgo's rock era.

Phainon paused.

Wait, that… can’t be Robin, right?

But when the song played on, and she hit the high notes, it was clear that it is Robin. Phainon raised his brows, almost whistling in admiration, but held himself back not to add an unnecessary voice to the otherwise perfect song.

Then, the next song played, and it was just as bold as the previous one. This one even had a hint of a challenging, seductive voice. Phainon could almost know which Gorgo’s song inspired this; one of Mydei’s favorite songs, too. The one that Phainon had said he wanted to play as their angry make-out song, but rejected with a yell about “I will not do anything filthy with you with my mom’s voice in the background”, and a punch that left him bruised for days.

Then, the last song played. This one was bold, theatrical, thunderous, and uncharacteristically confident for Robin. It was more than a song inspired by Queen Gorgo. It felt like this track was meant to be written for Queen Gorgo herself in her prime, and at the same time, it also sounded the closest to Robin compared to the other tracks. The energy of her singing was contagious; it made you want to dance, join in with her 'ooooh lalala,' and would definitely be a concert climax.

That song was such a statement, as if Robin was entering Queen Gorgo’s castle, placing a laurel on her own head, and giving the entire place a new dawn with her voice. But instead of claiming the throne, she stood on the other side of the Queen, completing the image of royalty that had only ever been the Queen… and her son, Mydeimos.

Phainon could almost see where the idea of a fake relationship came from.

“The Rock Princess,” Phainon whispered to himself, at the same time that the song ended. Making her voice the only one breaking the silence.

His quiet commentary was welcomed with a booming laugh from Aventurine.

“Clever observation, Okhema,” Aventurine said. For the first time, acknowledging Phainon as a person and not just some unwanted mosquito. “It made her a different kind of princess. So you understand why I’m uneasy, right?”

No, Phainon did not understand. For him, it was good to show that Robin had an extensive range of creativity. She’s more than just a studio-made pop star. She’s a talented artist who drew inspiration from a legendary musician and created an entirely new genre.

What’s so catastrophic about it?

“You’re afraid that this change of genre would be rejected harshly by the fans,” Mydei suddenly spoke. “So you want to parade it behind a fake relationship with the son of Queen Gorgo. Because then, if people come to hate this, if the response did not fit your expectation, you could just frame the whole album as a love-driven experiment. A pop princess pulled by the magnetic charm of a rock boy, entered her rebellious phase, and strayed from her sparkly castle to make a few songs out of love. You could write off the whole thing as just a phase—an influence of a man she has an infatuation with. If it doesn’t work out, you could break us up, and you could usher her back to Clockie Castle, where she could continue making pop music for the young girls.”

Mydei paused, staring right at Aventurine as he continued.

“You want me there as the damage control.”

Mydei spoke it in a flat tone, with no emotions present whatsoever. However, his brutal observation seemed to freeze the room, revealing the cold intention behind the collaboration. Robin pressed her lips and closed her eyes in surrender, looking like she did not want to be there at all. Aglaea let out a little smile, looking proud that Mydei had noticed something she must have seen since this Aventurine guy approached her the first time.

While Aventurine whistled.

“Brawn, Beauty, Brain,” he said, in the same light tone and bright smile, despite his plan just being outed so brutally. “Please save something for the rest of us mortals, Mydeimos. It’s not hurt to not be perfect for once, I assure you.”

Mydei did not answer him. He was still silent, and his face was void of expression, but his tightened hold on Phainon’s hand was enough of a giveaway for Phainon to understand what he truly felt.

“That’s more or less summarizes it, but I wouldn’t call it damage control, when this collaboration will benefit you the most. Robin did not just write a song inspired by your Mother. She invented a genius masterpiece. A whole album of it. She will bring the golden rock era from your mother to life, while giving it modern touches. It will be a fresh start for the rock-and-roll world. She would continue your mother’s voice that screams at the girls to own their femininity, be bold, and pursue the guys or girls they have crushes on. It’s empowering to the young audience, while also expanding the demographic for Sons of Gorgo. Make your band even more massive by targeting the young women’s market. Do you know how well that market is doing? They would literally buy anything, even badly formulated cosmetics, so long as they have your name on it.”

Aventurine was straight-up speaking nonsense now. Phainon could not even follow his own train of thought, aside from the fact that this man could not wait to cash in on those songs, milking every last bit of money he could make from them, while also benefiting from the PR insurance. That sounds remarkably similar to capitalism, in bold and black letters. But Aglaea raised her brows, and Mydei did not respond. Perhaps he’s onto something.

“And I haven’t even mentioned how it would benefit you. You will greatly benefit from Robin’s exposure. She had three times as many followers on Chrystagram, almost a billion views on TabTube; you will be the sexiest rockstar of the decade. Dating Robin would increase your charisma. You’ll be granted the title of sexiest man alive. The ladies would be all over you.”

Mydei scoffed. “Yeah, except I’m literally—.”

“Bisexual,” Anaxa and Aglaea retorted in unison, a rehearsed white lie they crafted at the beginning of Mydei’s career to keep him safe from the prejudices in the underground scene. Phainon did not mind. Status rarely means anything to him. He knew Mydei, and they had begun their relationship with openness and complete honesty from the start.

Mydei scoffed. “Whatever. That last part wasn’t necessary at all. I don’t care about sex appeal,”

“But you do agree those are amazing songs,” Aventurine pressed.

“Yes. The riffs are banger. Who did that?”

“Me,” Robin smiled. “I could play guitar too.”

“Huh,” Mydei hummed. “That’s sick.”

Robin nodded with a tiny blush, looking like she was proud of getting recognition from Mydei. She was genuine about this, Phainon could tell. And he thought it would be a harmless, even fun thing to do, if only that Aventurine guy did not spin it in that way just to make sure she could come out of it without a scratch, should her experiment fail.

It made the collaboration thing sound more sinister than it actually is.

But if Phainon thought about it, despite his questionable method, Aventurine might not be a terrible person. He was just a brilliant PR guy trying to accommodate his client. Perhaps just lacking a little (or a lot!) in the empathy department.

But again, perhaps the marketing people wouldn’t be great at their job if they weren’t a little bit morally grey.

Phainon just wondered how it would be for Mydei if the public didn’t like that collaboration at all. Would he be the one paying for the downfall?

“What about him?” Phainon suddenly asked. He still felt like he didn’t belong, and Aventurine’s gaze still made him feel small, but he pressed on. “If this thing failed, what about Mydei and the band?”

“I understand where that worry comes from, but the whole thing will be carefully crafted to protect everyone’s image,” Robin’s brother said. His tone was calm, less flashy than Aventurine’s, but no less persuasive. “As Mister Aventurine mentioned, we’ve ensured this collaboration will benefit both parties. I know it may seem like we’re trying to use you as a fallback if things don’t go well—which, for the record, I truly doubt. The music Robin just shared was phenomenal. And she created it out of deep respect for you and your mother’s legacy. With your creative input, I believe it could be even more extraordinary. This arrangement serves only as both a precaution and a strategic promotional move.”

He cleared his throat, his gaze softening with a quiet melancholy as he continued.

“In an ideal world, I would give a Robin complete freedom to explore her artistry however she chooses without having to involve an outside party. However, right now, Clockie Studios relies heavily on her fame. Thousands of people work under that name. It’s my job to make sure Robin’s creative evolution doesn't jeopardize anyone’s livelihood. I know it’s not perfect, but… sometimes a small white lie is the only way to move things forward without closing any doors.”

Wow.

Talking about being persuasive.

It was either Robin’s brother had somehow learned of Mydei’s kindness to use it against him, or he was just a man sharing Mydei’s values for his people’s economy.

Because it hit Mydei right at his core, Phainon knew that. The only reason Mydei continued to perform at all, aside from his love for music and his mother’s legacy, was that there were people whose livelihoods depended on his fame. His five bandmates and their families, the Kremnoan people he hired as roadies or crew, and the individuals in the Kremnoan tourism industry who gained popularity after Mydei became a hit rockstar.

Aglaea must have noticed it too, because then she added. "Sunday spoke the truth, Mydei. I've reviewed the proposed PR plan thoroughly, and I do think it would serve us rather well," Aglaea said. "They've got the contingency sorted, and our team will ensure we come out of this without a scratch to your reputation. That said, this is entirely your call. We will not be moving forward with any of it unless you're on board."

Mydei only responded to Aglaea with a nod. “Alright,” he said, finally. “I only have two conditions to agree with this plan. First, I will get the final say on the narrative. It’s my mother’s legacy. A single bad story about her, and I will quit the whole thing.”

“Absolutely,” Robin answered. “I am only doing it out of respect for her, and to carry on her music, I promise. I will not proceed if it harms her image in any way, either.”

Mydei nodded in her direction again.

“And second,” he said again, no less authoritative than the first one. “I will not do this if my partner has even the slightest discomfort about the plan.”

Phainon nodded. Yeah, that’s so reasonable and diplomatic of him to wish for his partner’s approval. After all, a public fake relationship sounded like…

Wait.

Wait, wait, wait, wait.

It’s him. Phainon.

Phainon is Mydei’s partner.

He must state his agreement, isn’t he?

Damn that Mydeimos bastard. So when he said that he needed Phainon to be here, it was quite in a literal sense, not some kind of romantic, moment-of-vulnerability thing as Phainon had thought. Damn you, Mydeimos. You’re so lucky, you’re super cute, and you have a nice ass.

Aventurine scoffed. “Sure, if you could put your boyfriend on the phone…”

“Phainon,” Mydei nudged his shoulder, ignoring Aventurine. Again. “Now you’ve heard ‘em. What do you think?”

For the first time since they entered the room, Phainon could feel the gazes of all people zeroed in on him. He raised his brows, suddenly feeling hyper aware of himself and the bad fashion he wore because Mydei had refused to let him get out of bed all day yesterday. Aventurine narrowed his eyes at him, looking suspicious.

“Wait, I Love Okhema is your boyfriend?” Aventurine raised his voice, sounding scandalized. “Wow, rockstars do have weird taste in partners.”

Aventurine’s unnecessary jab at his fashion made Phainon even more self-aware. Bastard. Phainon was sure not to let Mydei get away with this. He’s super lucky that Phainon is head over heels for him—

His thought was interrupted when their eyes met, and Phainon momentarily forgot about his personal vendetta. He was far too distracted by Mydei’s golden eyes and how serious he looked.

He was being serious. He genuinely asked Phainon’s opinion about it.

And if Phainon knew anything about Mydeimos (he knows everything), he could see that Mydei was not actually opposed to the idea of this collaboration, as strange as it might be. Mydei had always wanted his mother’s music to be heard by as many people as it could, her legacy and message to be carried as far as possible. Queen Gorgo was a huge hit in the rockstar scene back in her day. She was predicted to be the next big thing, but then she was pregnant with Mydei, and she quit the scene altogether, promising to return with a Prince who knew exactly how to rock. But then, she passed away when Mydei was still very young.

The music industry was in grief at her passing. They called her a star dimmed too soon, an undethroned queen, basically put her on a pedestal for years. Mydei lowkey blamed himself for that. He still did now, hence his ambition to carry on his Mother’s legacy.

And everyone in the room knows that if it comes to promotion, nothing in the world is bigger than Robin. She was the biggest platform they could get.

That reason was an enticing enough offer on its own. Adding Robin’s phenomenal tracks on top of it was definitely a one-in-a-million chance. Something that other celebrities might be willing to kill for. But Phainon knew that the music was what moved Mydei into agreement. Phainon saw how he was when they played the songs. He enjoyed them. Phainon could see how much he liked them, even under the mask of nonchalance that he wore so perfectly.

On paper, it was probably one of the best offers not only for Mydei nor the band, but also for Chrysos Records.

Still, with that much at stake, Mydei placed the final decision in Phainon’s hands. Phainon. The last person in the room who knows anything about music, legacy, or fame.

Oh.

Was that why Mydei was so stressed about it back in the car? Was he worried about Phainon’s thoughts? Did he have that much value in their relationship as much as he values his own ambition?

Aww.

Damn this man and his cute determination and his cute butt. Phainon wanted to cry.

Is it considered voyeurism if he kissed him right here and now?

Aventurine cleared his throat, definitely trying to get Phainon out of his own thoughts.

Bastard. But well, thank you for that.

“Ahem. I mean, if you want to do it, then go ahead, ‘Dei,” Phainon said. “That sounds cool. Your mom would really love it if she’s still around.”

“The fake-relationship part, HKS,” Mydei hissed.

“Alright, alright, I’m getting there, be patient,” Phainon replied. “I’m okay with that, too. Don’t worry about it. I mean, as I said, it’s just what celebrities do, right? Make headlines, give them a story? I mean, it sounds like a solid one, if you ask me. And for a better cause than we thought, too.”

Pahinon gave Mydei a reassuring smile; the joke he threw carelessly at the car just now lingered in his voice, and Mydei smiled at him in return.

“I must be sure, though,” Phainon said, shifting his eyes to Robin’s brother (Sunday?), Aventurine, then Aglaea. “This will not hurt Mydei, right? His reputation, his music, himself, nothing?”

“It will not, I promise,” Robin’s brother, Sunday, said. “We will make sure the campaign goes smoothly, I can promise you that.”

“Right,” Phainon nodded. “But if it hurts him in any way, or makes him uncomfortable, I will stop agreeing with this. Okay? You must stop it immediately.”

Phainon turned to Mydei on the last part of his words, which was welcomed with Mydei’s lopsided smirk. Like he was proud of him.

“Alright,” he said as he squeezed Phainon’s hand. “The same goes the other way around. The moment it made Phainon uncomfortable, I would stop it too.”

“Aww, stop being so sweet, you two. My teeth will decay,” Aventurine clapped his hand, and Phainon could still hear him muttering I love Okhema? Really? Under his breath, before he continued. “Then in that case, let’s go over the details.”

Robin gave them the biggest smile, and her eyes lit up with hope and unmistakable joy, as beautiful as the first ray of the morning sun. Phainon couldn’t help but trust her to take care of Mydei throughout the act. She seemed to know her way around Aventurine’s schemes, and her love for music seemed to be so unmistakable.

By Kephale, Phainon hoped he did not just make a mistake.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Blow Me Away
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

As Aventurine's plan unfolded, Phainon had an absolute thrill watching it unfold. He did not doubt Mydei. He knew their love was strong. Until he witnessed a few loose ends that he tried to ignore.

Chapter Notes

Hiii! I hope you enjoy this as much as I enjoy writing it. the title of the chapter, as usual, is taken from the song it took inspiration from, "Blow Me Away" by Breaking Benjamin ft Valora. I thought this song is perfect for Mydei and Robin's duet :D

The meeting was… well, weird.

Phainon expected to be ushered out once he had given Mydei his approval of the plan. But apparently, Aventurine had gone back to considering him as an irrelevant mosquito as he presented his ‘roadmap’ of how this Robin Goes Rock ‘campaign’ would go for the next six months.

After ten minutes, Phainon gave up pretending to understand all of his marketing jargon and returned to the game on his phone. He was positive that Mydei would fill him in later, using simplified language he would definitely understand.

Though he did turn his attention back to the screen when Aventurine mentioned Robin’s and Mydei’s Moodboard, curious about what that was.

Apparently, it was a board filled with images, color palettes, and bullet points of how Robin would appear in public during her time “dating” Mydei. The outfit, the makeup, the accessories—every detail was meticulously planned.

Robin must always wear a bright inner layer: soft, pastel-toned chiffon or satin blouses in flowing silhouettes, dresses with gentle pleats, the kind that swayed delicately when she walked. The outerwear, however, was where the “rock” came in—cropped leather jackets, chunky bangles, platform boots, all in black or dark purple metallics. Only the top layer was allowed to be rebellious. The core of her fashion—the part closest to her body—had to remain feminine and bright.

Her makeup followed the same philosophy. No full black eyeliner, no heavy shadows. She would wear bright, translucent makeup with white or lavender eyeshadow over the lids, and a smoky gradient only at the outer edges; all the dark shades were concentrated on the outside, as if they had been placed there by an external influence.

“It’s a narrative layering for Robin,” Aventuine explained, swiping to the next slide in the confidence that told them he was very proud of his creation. “We’re keeping her core and adding the tension to it. The passion of young love, the admiration for the brave new world, which is completely different from her own. Mydei’s influence was engulfing her, protecting her.”

Phainon blinked slowly.

No, the way he saw it, that’s not how it looked at all.

Phainon knew nothing about Public Relations, but from what Aventurine had presented, he could only see that Robin’s rock persona was meant to be detachable; it was all outer accessories she could take off at the end of the night, and when things did not work out, her pop princess image stayed untouched.

Huh.

Before Phainon could say anything, Aventurine moved to Mydei’s moodboard. It was much simpler. Just his usual chaotic rocker aesthetic with hidden easter eggs tucked in: faded Clockie Studios shirt, a dove feather pendant on his necklace, a treble clef charm on his leather bracelet,

a small Robin-styled star on his favorite jackets, a silver star sticker on his guitar instead of the sun sticker—

“No,” Mydei said sharply. “The guitar and the sun sticker are off limits.”

“I see,” Aventurine hummed. “But maybe…”

“Off. Limits.”

“Alright,” Aventurine bit his tongue, his lips curved in a lopsided smirk as he made the tiniest glance at Phainon’s neck; probably at his sun tattoo that slightly resembled the one on Mydei’s guitar. “Noted.”

Then came the timeline: Mydei and Robin would start working on Robin’s tracks in two days, adding Mydei’s creative elements, with Anaxa and Dr. Ratio also joining in to co-produce the songs. Mydei had suggested putting it all together into one EP, to which Robin wholeheartedly agreed.

After the music, Aventurine also revealed how they would make news. In the first week, Robin would post a social media post of her breakfast with Mydei’s hand blurred in the background, then they were “caught” by Paparazzi getting out of a beachside restaurant in South Golden Hour. In the next few days, Robin would wear one of Mydei’s shirts, preferably from Mydei’s famous paparazzi photo, so the fans could easily connect the dots. Mydei would say something vague in a radio interview about “unexpected muses.” These weren’t obvious—just enough for obsessive fans to connect the dots in theory threads and “spot the reference” videos.

Phainon still wasn’t sure there would be people lifeless enough to connect the dots from them, let alone make theories and gossip. But again, it wasn’t his world. Phainon zoned out until a photoshopped image of Robin and Mydei at the Net Gala came to the screen.

They would attend as a couple, stealing the headlines, with so many reporters and media covering the event. Robin would wear a Gorgo-inspired dress, while Mydei donned a suit that matched her aesthetic. Not a matchy-matchy couple outfit per se; Robin would still wear her bright, sparkly colors. But their outfit must make a statement about the ‘Royal Couple’.

Phainon gaped, feeling a mix of unease and secondhand claustrophobia.

Mydei had received the invitation to the gala, Phainon knew as much. Aglaea had also proposed a few designs of the outfit he would be wearing; Phainon also knew about that. What he didn’t know was that they had secretly matched it with Robin. It was as if they had planned it much earlier than ‘a couple of days’.

The moodboard, the dress, the songs…

How long had they planned about this?

He glanced at Mydei, who was still staring at the screen, looking bored and nodding along like he was mentally five floors above this conversation. He did not look shocked, nor was he even slightly fazed. He seemed completely fine, listening to Aventurine outline where he would be, what he would wear, and how he would behave over the next six months.

Phainon turned to Robin and saw that she looked just as calm despite having her identity sliced into digestible bullet points and moodboard colors. She even chimed in with a few suggestions, pointing out where they could subtly echo Queen Gorgo’s tour legacy, especially in the second quarter of the campaign. She looked a bit excited about the whole thing.

Perhaps this was normal, Phainon thought. Perhaps this was just how it worked in this celebrity world. They’re completely okay having their identity written down and planned out like a premonition.

Phainon remained silent and returned to his phone. He's gotta find another chest to round up his stars to 160 anyway. He almost hit enough pity to get the Fig Stew chimera.

The meeting ended around thirty minutes later, just right when Phainon got enough stars to finally try his luck on the Fig Stew banner. Mydei nudged Phainon’s chair, signaling him to get out. But just as Phainon wanted to get up from his chair, Robin approached them.

Wait, no, not them

Him.

Robin approached him. Phainon.

“Hello, can I have a moment of your time, please? My name is Robin, pleasure to meet you, um, Mister…”

Robin extended her hand for a handshake, to which Phainon could only stare in awe, unsure how to behave in front of such a famous person, whom he had seen on TV since he was in school. He blinked, completely starstruck as words refused to form on his tongue.

Mydei elbowed him, sobering him up.

“Oh, uh… yeah, right, Robin. Phainon. My name… is Phainon. Nice to meet you,” he said, giving Robin a quick handshake, and wow, so this is what it feels like touching an angel. Her hands were smooth, she smelled nice, and she was positively glowing, holy shit. “Um… and yes, Robin. I know you. I played a knight in my school play and sang your song.”

Phainon said that to cover his nervousness, but it sounded too awkward and robotic. He could hear Mydei snicker next to him, but thankfully, Robin did not join him in the laugh and nodded instead.

“I see, that sounds wonderful. I guess since we will be seeing each other more often, you could tell me about the play later? That must be a fun experience,” she said. “Oh, and please, no need to be so formal. I will be in your care from now,” she made a slight bow, a very graceful one, and Phainon nodded.

“Sure,” he said. He patted himself for not stammering. His mouth was dry, and he was nervous as fuck. Man, he’s not even into women, but by Kephale, this lady’s charm was something else. “Please also take care of Mydei. He could be… uh, a handful,” he continued, glancing at Mydei, who was just rolling his eyes.

“Let’s go home, HKS,” Mydei said, before turning to Robin. “We’ll be going ahead, Miss.”

“Oh, sure, please, don’t let me keep you,” Robin said. “Thank you again for being willing to do this with me, Mydei. It means so much to me. Please take care on your way home.”

“What’s the rush, boys? Come on, join us in the celebratory kickoff dinner,” Aventurine suddenly joined in the conversation, with his bright, cunning smile and his relaxed mannerism that somehow made Phainon a little bit stiff. “I know a lovely place downtown. Very private, super tasty food, my treat. You won’t regret it.”

Phainon glanced at Mydei, who only shrugged, not even thinking twice before rejecting. “No thanks, we already have a plan.”

“Come onnnn, it’ll be…”

“This isn’t in your plan, right?” Mydei interrupted. Again. Phainon bit back a smile. Aventurine had to start getting used to it. “I didn’t see it on your presentation deck, so no, we will not be joining. Thank you for the invitation, though.”

Aventurine opened his mouth, closed it for a moment, then chuckled. “Alright, I’ll see you at Golden Hour in a week, then,” he said, flashing a bright smile as he nodded. “Oh, but, Okhema, one more thing.”

“Phainon,” Mydei retorted. But his eyes were still on Aventurine, narrowing in a way that made Phainon a little bit… well, surprised.

“What?” Phainon whispered, wondering why Mydei had suddenly called him.

“His name is Phainon,” Mydei continued. His eyes were still locked onto Aventurine.

Oh.

He corrected Aventurine in a cold, flat tone that he usually reserved for people he did not like. Phainon had only seen this attitude when Mydei met an uncle from his father’s side. It scared him… a little. Phainon hadn’t seen

Mydei like this for a while. He was usually just aloof or curt, but rarely intimidating.

Phainon wondered if Mydei was also a little wary of Aventurine, and if this was his defense mechanism.

“If we’re gonna do this, you better respect him and address him properly because no way I’m gonna do any of your shit if he’s not being treated well.”

Aventurine did not back off. He met Mydei’s stare with lazy eyes, challenging him head-on despite Mydei’s arm looking bigger than Aventurine’s thigh, or that Mydei was a whole head taller than him.

This guy looked eerily fearless.

It made Phainon even more uneasy because a tough, muscular guy being challenging was one thing, but it was a whole different level when a petite, sleek guy was doing that. It felt like he knew nothing that the rest of them didn’t, and you could never be safe with him.

“Alright, Phainon,” he said, finally breaking his gaze from Mydei and shifting to talk to Phainon directly, flashing a polite smile and cheerful attitude. “Apologies for my whole… impudence today. You see, I’m really on the edge with the entire… Robin Goes Rock thing,” he let out a laugh. No pressure, no awkwardness at all. As if they were all just an old friend enjoying an old joke that everyone was familiar with.

Except that they didn’t, and it was weird as heck.

“But well, I’m glad your approval now helps us run things. I will take care of this just right, don’t worry. Your boyfriend is in good hands. Although I have just one more thing I need from you, before we part ways today…”

Phainon nodded. “Sure,” he replied, a little bit curious about what he could do to help Mydei, but mostly he just wanted this to be over soon, so he could go back to their apartment and enjoy the weekend together, as it was so rare to come by these days.

“I’m sure this goes without saying, but I would sleep better at night if you promise to keep this whole thing confidential, okay?” Aventurine smiled. “I talk about best friends, siblings, even nieces or nephews. People outside of this little tight-knit band of ours. After all, the success of this campaign relies solely on the complete control of the narrative. It would be easier for Mydei, too, if there were no unnecessary complications.”

Phainon did not know whether he was supposed to be offended or what that meant. But Aventurine was giving him his genuine smile, not the smug one. So he nodded, returning the hospitality in full.

“Sure, I will definitely remember that, Mister Aventurine,” he said. “Please let me know if there’s anything else I can do to help Mydei and Miss Robin in this project. I will happily do so.”

Aventurine answered with a "thank you, absolutely,” but before he could say anything more, Mydei interrupted him, saying they had somewhere to be and really needed to go.

And just like that, they got out of Aglaea’s office, taking the elevator down to the parking lot and finally back in the safety of their car.

Mydei leaned back to the passenger’s seat, groaning loudly as he covered his eyes with his arm. “By strife’s name, I hate PR people.”

Phainon chuckled. “You did well, ‘Dei,” he said as he rubbed Mydei’s shoulder, giving him an empathetic hum as Mydei leaned into his touch. “Didn’t even look like you’re going to stab that Aventurine guy. Well, you did a little, though, but overall, nice job.”

“I gotta be. He would’ve sunk his teeth in deeper if he smelled any of my emotion back then,” Mydei mumbled. “One thing I learned from Aglaea is that if the PR people start talking, you'd better not give them anything, especially emotions. They knew their way around it. Someone like Aventurine would know even better and use that to get to you.”

“Hmm, coming from Aglaea, that's gotta be some real shit,” Phainon nodded. “But, why did you drag me in there, ‘Dei? Isn’t it like… showing

your trump card to the enemy or something? Like, the way you acted, Aventurine would know that he could get you through me now.”

Mydei peeked at him from behind his arm.

“Yeah, and that’s precisely the point I want to get across. I want him to know that whatever shit he wants me to do in his circus, you will have a say in it. So whatever it is he and Aglaea are planning, they will not just consider how it would affect Robin, me, or the band, but also how it could affect you.” he paused, and Phainon could see a slight tug on Mydei’s lips as he continued. “Also, I want you to stop being naive for once and understand how important your decision would be in this.”

Phainon raised his brows. “Me? Naive?”

Mydei gave him a look.

“I’m not naive!”

“Hephaestion once joked that he could kiss me in one music video to make a hit, and you said, ‘okay, if it’s good for the band’.”

Phainon gaped, starting the engine as he said, “Well…” That was not wrong. “Fine. But what was I supposed to say? I’m not just gonna keep you from success out of mere jealousy.”

Mydei rolled his eyes. “This is exactly why I brought you in there, HKS. This time, it’s not a Hephaestion joke you could just shrug off. This is big, and we can’t always control the output. I want you to know what we’ve gotten into, and you have to be honest about how you feel about this entire situation. I could always find a way to honor Mom’s music. But the music, the legacy, they’re not more important than you. You hear that?”

He sounded serious, his heavy voice thickened by the silence in the car, like he wanted to hammer every syllable down to Phainon’s skull. Like he always did when he talked about his parents.

Phainon hummed, allowing the silence to stretch a little more before nodding.

“Alright,” Phainon said, grabbing Mydei’s hand and placing it above the gear. “I’m truly fine with it, don’t worry. I know how fake that was. Aventuine had designed everything to the point that I won’t even have room to be surprised. I’ve known every small bit you would say and do in that scenario,” he chuckled. “If anything, it’s kind of exciting, you know? It must be hilarious to see how people react to those small clues Aventurine has placed. Though I also wanna see him fume when his plan fails. He seems very confident about how people will respond to those tiny clues. I don’t think people will have that much time to make theories out of celebrities.”

Mydei winced. “You’ll be surprised by what people on the internet can do.”

Phainon raised his brows. “Really? Then it’ll even be hilarious to watch. Like a worldwide virtual easter egg hunt, except I know what the actual catch is.”

Mydei’s lips tugged a little. “Yeah, you could do that,” he said. “But anyway, thank you for allowing me to do this.”

Phainon shrugged. “It’s fine, ‘Dei. You know I’m always here to support you,” he said. “Though I hope I won’t ever cross paths too much with that Aventurine. Dude totally creeped me out.”

Mydei scoffed. “You’re scared of someone smaller than you? Loser.”

“He’s almost half your size, yet he met your eye to eye. There’s something crazy-scary about small guys with that kind of guts, y’know? It feels like he knows something we don’t. Besides, he looked like… uh…”

“Sly fox? Shark?”

“No,” Phainon said. “Like the embodiment of capitalism.”

Mydei laughed again, this time louder. “You’re so dumb,” he said. “But that wasn’t wrong.”

“I know, right?” Phainon hummed. “But again, I think it means he’s really good at his job. And there’s Aglaea, Anaxa, and Robin’s brother, too. I know they’re decent people. Aglaea and Anaxa are, at least. And Robin is a literal angel. So I could trust that you’re in such capable hands. I wouldn’t have room to be worried about anything at all.”

Mydei grunted. “Hmm.”

“It’s just six months, anyway, right?”

“Yeah,” Mydei said. “It is. But just remember you got that safe word, ‘kay? Whenever you feel uncomfortable. Just say the word, and I’ll stop. You know how I mean it.”

“Mmm,” Phainon hummed. “You’re always so attentive to my safe words.”

“HKS, this is serious,” Mydei glared at him.

“Oh, sorry, I thought we already broke the ice when we talked shit about your PR maven guy,” Phainon chuckled. “But fine, I hear you. For now, do you want Honeycake takeout? After all of that, no way I’m gonna allow you to the kitchen…”

“Yes!” Mydei replied quickly. “Yes, please!”

-

The rest of their weekends were not as eventful. Phainon had the Sunday he wanted with Mydei, cooking home meals together (well, Mydei did most of the actual cooking, while Phainon “helped” by sliding behind him, pressing his chest against Mydei’s back, and stealing kisses under the collar of his

shirt). He did the easier prep work—chopping vegetables, licking sauce off his boyfriend’s fingers, deliberately driving Mydei to the brink of patience.

“Try to do that once again, and I will just give up this food and watch you die of starvation,” Mydei had said, with a real annoyance in his voice. Despite the dark in his eyes, he looked like he actually wanted to finish the cooking.

“Keep bluffing,” Phainon taunted. “You know you love keeping me full.”

But despite his teasing, Phainon left Mydei to finish cooking and eating lunch together. Then, they caught up on their backlog of movies. They half-watched some, fully ignored others—especially once Phainon pulled Mydei onto his lap and dragged him into a slow, open-mouthed kiss that left no room for popcorn, only hands and heat and skin against skin, and the determination to tend to each other’s insatiable needs.

Time flew by so fast when Phainon had Mydei in his arms, because the next thing they knew, the sun had dipped entirely below the horizon, leaving them alone in the dim light of their room, with their regulated breaths being the only sound.

The last hours of their free time together always felt bittersweet for Phainon. It always felt so wholesome, because as the weight of temporary separation loomed above them, Mydei would get a little bit… sentimental, for lack of better words. His emotions would clash and be unleashed in the most feral yet sweetest ways possible. His kisses would be deep with hunger, but they lingered like a promise. His touches would be rough, yet they wandered like a brush mapping Phainon’s shapes for his keepsake, and his eyes…

His eyes would stare at him in challenge, in lust, in pride, and yet, as Phainon dived deeper, he would find the warmth and light that was just enough to rekindle his soul.

And as the night ended against their will, Mydei would curl against him, his hand inside Phainon’s. He would press his back against Phainon’s chest like

he hoped he could freeze them in time, but knew that because he couldn’t, he’d soaked in Phainon’s presence before morning light forced them apart.

It was cute to see such a child-like determination in the usually proud man. It made Phainon feel honored that Mydei allowed him to know that part of him. But it was also heartbreaking, knowing that it would be days, weeks, or even months before they could be this close again. Before Phainon could see this side of him again, and not the aloof rockstar who speaks profanities on video interviews or screams his lungs out on stage.

And with Mydei’s recording session and summer tour coming up, Phainon knew that it might probably be months, this time.

Phainon drifted to a dreamless sleep. With Mydei so close to him like that, it’s rare for Phainon to dream, knowing that he had everything he had ever wanted in this world in his embrace. When he slowly stirred from slumber, he could tell from the red glow bleeding through his eyelids that dawn had arrived: the moment to temporarily part had arrived.

Phainon pressed his lips to the back of Mydei’s neck, even before opening his own eyes, just to catch him before the world did. He inhaled the smell of Mydei’s hair; his natural scent and faint smell of his shampoo lingered in his nose, and he nuzzled against the other’s neck as the minutes dragged him further away from their small heaven, closer to the day with responsibilities.

When their bedside clock beeped, Mydei stirred, a low whine escaping his throat as he instinctively arched his back, pressing his body closer to Phainon in the same manner a little boy sank deeper into his blanket on a school day. His fingers fumbled for Phainon’s wrist, as if trying to keep him there a little longer.

“Morning, princess,” Phainon whispered against the curve of Mydei’s jaw, voice rough with sleep. He pressed a soft kiss there, lingering longer than usual. “Wanna join me for a shower?”

Mydei's response was a sleepy growl full of lazy protest and a firmer grip on his hand. “Stay.”

Phainon chuckled quietly. “Hey, now,” he said, even as his own body wanted nothing more but to obey Mydei’s words. “I gotta go, or else I’m gonna be late.”

“Stay,” Mydei repeated—this time with the petulance of a boy trying to will the sun back down. His voice was thick with sleep and grief tangled up together.

Phainon shifted, rising just enough to plant a kiss on Mydei’s cheek, then another on the corner of his eye, mirroring the tattoo on his left eye. Mydei made a weak protest sound. He still wouldn’t let go of Phainon’s fingers, holding them hostage in a lazy but determined grip.

“Alright, then, keep holding on to me,” Phainon chuckled again, pressing another kiss on Mydei’s nose. “If you really want to be dragged to the cold shower so badly.”

Mydei grunted, but eventually, he loosened his grip, letting Phainon slip away.

When Phainon got out of the shower, Mydei had dozed back off. His soft snore accompanied Phainon as he got ready for the day, dressing in his uniform, packing the few things he needed for the trip, zipping his suitcase, putting on his perfume, and reheating Mydei’s cooking for a quick breakfast. He would have wanted Mydei to join him, but Mydei looked so spent that Phainon did not have the heart to wake him. So Phainon ate alone and allowed Mydei to sleep a little longer.

Though he did not leave without saying goodbye, knowing Mydei would hate waking up to an empty house. So he kneeled on Mydei’s side of the bed and kissed the tip of his nose.

“Hey, sleeping beauty,” he whispered. “Wake up. I really have to leave.”

Mydei stirred in his sleep, opening an eye and stretching like a graceful lion, and frowned as he stared at Phainon. “You don’t have to go to work,” he grunted, his voice still groggy with sleep, but there was a hint of sadness

in there; the specific gloom that was always shown whenever one of them had to leave for work. “You could be my trophy husband.”

Phainon laughed softly, brushing hair from Mydei’s temple to kiss the furrow that shaped between his brows.

“How about you become my trophy husband?” he said, then kissed Mydei on the cheek. On the chin. On the tip of his nose. Except on his lips, because if Phainon did that, it would be even harder to leave.

“What’s even the point of that?” Mydei grumbled, still with that childlike whine of his. “You’ll just leave me again. Over and over. If you were my trophy husband, you could be with me on tour. You can always travel with me, we’d be going places together. We don’t have to do this every few days.”

“Come on, now, it’s just a short regional leg this time. I’ll see you in two days, I promise,” Phainon said. Then, with a wicked grin, he continued. “You won’t be alone for long this time. Today you’re scheduled to debut as a pop princess’s boyfriend, remember?”

“Fuck you,” Mydei muttered, tossing a pillow half-heartedly in his direction.

Phainon laughed. “Is that a promise?”

“Get out. Go fly somewhere, I don’t care.”

Phainon caught the pillow and laughed, leaning in for one last peck on Mydei’s nose. But the blonde did not let up. He caught Phainon’s lips to kiss him—drawn out, final, reluctant.

Phainon almost didn't want to leave him, with how dearly Mydei held on to him. It always squeezed his heart, how this rockstar whom the people praised and idolized melted in his touch.

“What’s the word?” Phainon broke the kiss, much to Mydei’s frown.

“No.”

“Honeycake.”

“Stay.”

Phainon chuckled.

“Safe flight, HKS,” he whispered into the kiss, before pressing one more against Phainon’s lips. Then, another whisper. “Call me when you land.”

“I will,” Phainon promised, kissing him once more—a seal, a goodbye. His hand lingered on Mydei’s cheek, savoring the last few seconds it had before he had to let go.

And then he stood, suitcase in hand, walking out the door, carrying the warmth and the ache with him.

He closed the door quietly. Behind it, his heart stayed curled in a bed of messy sheets, wearing a sad smile and a sleepy whisper of love.

-

To Phainon’s dismay, he did not get to see Mydei again in two days as he had planned.

When he landed back in Okhema after his short regional flight, he heard the news that one of the senior pilots on his roster was suddenly hospitalized, and Phainon was the only one available to cover his leg of a long-haul route. Rivet Town, of all places. The flight schedule was brutal, and the layovers barely allowed time to breathe, let alone to come home. Phainon got stuck in the rotation until the weekend, surviving on airport hotels and tight turnarounds.

Even calling Mydei proved to be difficult. Their conversation was reduced to a quick “good morning” before his early briefings, or a rushed “good night, sleep tight” sent at six in the evening—because by the time Mydei

actually went to bed, Phainon would already be 30,000 feet above the continent.

Phainon did catch the photos Mydei sent when his phone was off, though; the image of Robin in the recording booth, giving a peace sign and an angelic smile. A short clip of a mixer application, giving Phainon a glimpse of music that Mydei was working on, Hephaestion’s selfie (definitely taken by Hephaestion himself when Mydei left his phone lying around), and more photos about the randomest things, like the sunset, his cooking, and a blurry picture of a cheerful Samoyed outside of Anaxa’s house / recording studio that Mydei captioned as “you” under.

Phainon returned it with photos of the hotel walls, the cockpit, his mirror selfie on the hotel’s mirror, and his catered breakfast. It was frustrating. Not just the exhaustion, but the gap that stretched longer between messages. Not because anything had gone wrong—just that they were too far apart, for too long, and the time zones were a bastard.

They had been doing this for years. Still, it didn’t make it any easier.

Phainon sighed with relief when he finally landed back in Okhema on Monday morning, already looking forward to his rest day as he dragged his suitcase out of the plane. Though, as he got out of the gate, he was suddenly welcomed with the image of his boyfriend…

In the airport television. Which, for some reason, showed Mydei instead of boring old people, probably world leaders, as he could always expect on an international news channel.

Mydei was shown in a slightly pixelated image, clearly taken from a distance. He was wearing his usual sunglasses, a black sleeveless shirt with a Clockie Studio large print, and a pair of worn-out black jeans. His blond hair was tied in a ponytail, while his braided hair hung free, held by small fingers that belonged to…

Robin.

She was wearing an oversized striped shirt that clearly did not belong to her, a pleated denim mini-skirt, and a pair of black Oxford shoes with frilly, cream-colored socks. Her hair was tied up, revealing her head wings completely. In the next photo, the news showed, Mydei placed his black baseball hat on Robin as they walked to Mydei’s car, apparently giving her a shield against the sun and probably the paparazzi. Her head wings perked up, like she was delighted.

Judging by the smile that the news portal zoomed in on, it was even clearer that she was, indeed, having fun.

Then, his eyes caught the title of the news.

Two Stars From Different Galaxies Collide in Romance?

Oh, Aventurine. The man that you are.

Phainon had to cover his lips with his fist, or else he would burst out laughing. He couldn’t hear what the presenter was saying over the airport noises, but they looked serious as they pointed out on Robin’s head, Mydei’s arm, and Kephale knows what else, looking like they were looking for signs.

Huh, so Aventurine’s plan was already in motion.

How long had it been? Phainon had truly lost track of time.

“Oh, sweet Kephale, so it’s real?”

Phainon could hear Nymphas, one of the flight attendants on his flight, exclaim. She tugged a friend next to her, pointing at the TV screen.

“Nereia, look. Robin and Mydeimos are officially an item now?”

“What, for real?” Nereia, another flight attendant, replied. She glanced at the screen and scoffed. “Pft, probably just a publicity stunt, Nymph. There’s no way Mydeimos would date someone like Robin. Isn’t she… too pop for him?”

Too girly, Phainon made a mental retort. Too girly and too Uptown. Mydei’s taste was more like a country boy. Specifically, a boy from Aedes Elysiae.

Nymphas shrugged. “Probably, but maybe it’s from Robin’s side? She had been a fan of Mydeimos since he debuted, after all!” she said, sounding too excited despite Nereia’s criticism. “My dear Mnestia, she must be really happy that they finally got to hang out like that. I mean, look at her smile! She’s beaming! Even her head wings perked up! When did the last time we saw her so happy like that?”

She was straight-up gushing now, and Phainon couldn’t help but approach them, intrigued by Nymphas’ apparent knowledge of the matter.

“Hi, ladies, what is it you’re talking about?” he asked. “Is it about Mydeimos and Robin?”

“Oh, Captain, hello!” Nymphas greeted him with a bright smile. “Are you following the news about them as well?”

“No, not so much. But I am somewhat of a fan of Robin, and I just caught the news of them together on TV just now. I’m curious about why she’s hanging out with Mydeimos. Isn’t he like, a totally different musician or something?” he replied. “What is it about them being in romance?”

Phainon was deliberately playing dumb now, and he felt a little bad about it. But his curiosity was enough to get Nymphas perked up, looking like she was glad to have someone to talk about it.

“No official statements yet, Captain. But it had been trending for a few days now. There’s a theory circulating on the internet about Robin finally getting to hang out with her long-standing celebrity crush. It was so cute!”

“Long-standing crush?” Phainon hummed, genuinely invested in her words now because Phainon did not know that. He did know that Robin was a fan of Mydei. He didn’t know that it was a crush or that it was a long-standing. “I thought she just liked their song?”

“She’s a fan of Sons of Gorgo, yes. But she’s also a total fangirl of Mydeimos since forever. In Sons of Gorgo's debut year, they won the Best Rock Artist. There’s an edit that shows Robin giving them a standing ovation, smiling wider than when she won Best Female Artist of the Year. Her eyes were glued to Mydeimos. There’s a video thread for that. I think people are still using her GIF as a reaction meme.”

Since forever, Phainon had repeated that in his mind and had taken a mental note to look for the video thread Nymphas mentioned.

“Then, when she won Best Song of the Year in that same year, she also said that her win was dedicated to all the artists in the nominations, including Sons of Gorgo. She mentioned them specifically! Oh, and she mentioned in a few interviews that Mydeimos’ fiery vocals helped lift the mood. She wore a Red Lion shirt in some paparazzi pictures, too! Red Lion was synonymous with Mydeimos, right?” Nympas added again.

She must have realized that she totally geeked out now, because then she cleared her throat and went back to her more serious self, looking a bit sheepish.

“I mean, it’s just so cute, you know? For her to finally get so close to the person she had had a celebrity crush on since forever. I couldn’t help but feel so happy for her. With Robin’s tight schedule, she rarely had time for personal stuff. She must finally have time for herself now that her Clockie Weekly Show wrapped up its final season.”

Phainon chuckled. “Don’t worry, I understand,” he said. “But what started the dating rumor?”

“There’s this Chrystagram Story on Robin’s account. It was not unusual; Robin was not very stingy in sharing her daily life. But on that particular post, there’s an arm of a man with a red tattoo in the background. It was too blurry, but some people matched it with Mydeimos’ arm tattoo, and the pattern was identical. Then there’s this live interview of Mydeimos at an event. He was wearing a chain necklace with a dove feather pendant that looked like it was Robin’s…”

“Mydeimos wears anything he likes. The internet is reading too much into it,” Nereia interrupted, huffing as they walked outside the exit gate. “It’s probably just something that some fans gave him. He likes to wear them in public to show he appreciates them.”

“No, no, but listen to this,” Nymphas said. “Yesterday, Mydeimos posted a Chrystagram Stories of him in the studio, and you know what the caption is?”

“A dove emoji,” Nereia answered. “Still, it didn’t mean anything.”

“That’s two clues hinting at doves, Nereia! Dove is the official emoji for Robin! Everyone knows that,” Nymphas said. “Captain is a Robin fan. You know that, right, Captain?”

Phainon did not know that, but he knows now, so he nodded. “Yeah, I guess?”

Nereia huffed. “I’m betting they’re just in a project together,” she said. “Mydeimos was not the type of person who liked his personal life to be under the spotlight. I mean, four years since debut and not a single dating rumor? That man knows how to keep a secret. This is probably a deliberate move. They’re probably just releasing something together. A duet, maybe. Not necessarily romance.”

Wow. Phainon was almost impressed by Nereia’s sensibility. He pressed his lips, trying so hard to bite back a smile. Wait until Aglaea or that Aventurine man hears about this.

“Hm,” Nymphas pouted. “Didn’t he have that… news about him with that bandmate of his?”

“Hepy? Oh, no, that was debunked quickly after. Hepy was just generally touchy, and they’re nothing but good friends.”

Ah. Now Phainon remembered that news. They thought Mydeimos and Hephaestion were a couple, back when Mydeimos first came out as bisexual (as per Aglaea’s direction), until they had to clarify that they’re

not. It was hilarious. Phainon still teased Mydei about it sometimes. Nereia seemed to know about Mydei’s stuff. She’s probably a huge fan of Mydei, as much as Nymphas is a massive fan of Robin.

Phainon almost wished he could give Nereia something related to Mydei. Probably a signed copy of his album or something. But he couldn’t risk exposing his connection to Mydei. They had strictly promised each other to keep their relationship a private matter when Mydei resigned his contract to Anaxa’s label.

“But, assuming that it’s real,” Nymphas insisted, bringing Phainon back to the ongoing conversation. “Don’t you think they look good together?”

Nereia paused for a bit, sighing in a way that she was resigning to Nymphas’ persistence. “Kind of?” she said. “It’s like a Dollywood Power Couple. You wouldn’t have a choice but to root for them.”

“Right? What do you think, Captain?” Nymphas asked him directly now, tilting her head in his direction to look at his expression.

Phainon did not even fake his smile and enthusiasm. “What Nereia said,” he replied. “I think they’re a perfect match for each other.”

Oh, the thrill of knowing something people don’t.

When they finally parted ways at the exit, and Phainon got a cab ride home, Phainon finally opened his phone and scrolled through the Dweetter app. True to Nymphas’ words, Mydei, Robin, and a hashtag called #LionDove were trending. Phainon clicked on the hashtag and was presented with more photos of Mydei and Robin in front of the Golden Hour restaurant. In a few pictures taken before they entered Mydei’s car, they were seen holding hands, and Mydei even smiled; his pristine white teeth, which Phainon loved to trace with his tongue, flashed for the camera.

He looked so beautiful.

And so did Robin next to him. They were a great contrast, but they looked so perfect together. Like the Dollywood Power Couple, as Nereia had called

it.

Phainon scrolled through the posts under the picture and read some of them.

@TimelyClockieDove A pair of music royalty from different sides of the music world, paired off to conquer the world. We never got a chance.

@mydeisguitarcase OMGGGG Shippp??? Ship ship ship!

@daughtersofgorgo Robin finally dating her celebrity crush is so inspiring. We could all date our celebrity crush, too, trust!

@mydeixmisia our ship had officially sunk. But congrats lovebirds!! Or should we say… lovecubs?

@Robindiehard Ew him? She’s too good for him.

@Mydeidiehard @robindiehard EXCUSE YOU??? He’s too rock and roll for the pop princess. He’s too good for her!!!

Phainon couldn’t help but laugh over the people arguing about how Robin and Mydei were not a good match, nodding over a theory that it was most likely a publicity stunt, but also amused by the theory that stated that it was, in fact, a real dating story. There was a story thread about it that called back Robin, mentioning Mydei over the past few years. Phainon watched every video, finally catching that Music Award moment that Nymphas talked about.

There was an edited video that included an explanatory line about Robin’s gaze, which was fixed directly on Mydei while she was giving her speech. As she mentioned Sons of Gorgo, her hand pointed in the general direction where the band sat, but her forefinger was pointed directly at Mydei. There was an interview on Good Morning Penacony! Show where Robin mentioned that she learned how to play the electric guitar for her newly

released movie by listening to Mydei’s guitar in Sons of Gorgo’s second album. Then there was a picture of her wearing white shirts featuring red lion-cub images, dating back to Sons of Gorgo's debut year.

It was hilarious how people had the time to collect all of those moments and place them together to support these dating allegations.

Mydei was right.

Aventurine does know what he’s doing.

Phainon only stopped scrolling when he finally got home. True to his suspicion, Mydei wasn’t home yet. He was probably already off to the studio. Phainon sent him a quick text to tell him that he’s already home, took a shower, and lay on his bed, planning to get some sleep to make up for his exhausting week, but he just couldn’t stop scrolling.

Phainon caught a few videos of Mydei in return, who had mentioned Robin in some way. It was far less than Robin mentioning Mydei, which makes it even more hilarious. There’s a video where they asked Mydei what he thinks about Robin in a red-carpet interview, to which Mydei hummed, “She’s super talented. She earned the fame she has now.” Which, in Mydei’s language (according to people), meant, “She’s incredible, I adore her, and she deserves all the love”.

Phainon was sure that in Mydei’s real language, it means that “I know who Robin is, but I don’t pay that much attention, and I want to go home.”
