Then, in a game show, when Mydei was asked where the lyrics came from, he correctly guessed Robin’s lyrics thrice, whereas the rest of his bandmates failed every time. The post said it meant Mydei was secretly a Robin’s big fan, but Phainon knew the reason Mydei got everything right was that Phainon sang those songs in the shower almost every day. He blasted them in their car. Mydei had no choice but to know the lyrics.

Then, when an interviewer asked Mydei what he thinks of Robin’s Lion Cub shirts, which were Sons of Gorgo official merchandise, Mydei said,

“It’s very kind of Robin to help promote our merch. Kudos,” and he was blushing while saying that.

Phainon couldn’t help but laugh out loud at that.

Mydei was not blushing. He was suffering from heatstroke. He spent almost two weeks in the cold winter of Jarilo’s Snowplains to shoot a video clip, and the sudden blast of Okhema’s summer heat was what made him blush.

Oh, this is gold.

Phainon now understood what Mydei meant when he told him about what people on the internet could do.

He took a couple of screenshots to tell (and tease) Mydei later. He was in the middle of watching a theory video about why Mydei and Robin would rule the music industry if the dating allegations were true when he heard his front door open.

Phainon did not even have time to jump out of bed to greet Mydei. When he entered the room, his guitar case on one shoulder and a bag of takeout that smelled suspiciously like Thai food. His shoulders drooped, with bags under his eyes, but a smile spread across his face as their eyes met.

“Hey,” he said, sounding as exhausted as he looked. Mydei dropped the guitar case and the takeout gently on the floor, and lay on the bed, his head on Phainon’s thigh.

“Hey, yourself,” Phainon said, getting up just enough to kiss Mydei.

“I thought you’d be sleeping,” Mydei said, tilting his head to Phainon’s gaze.

“I was gonna, but I was distracted by the news about Robin and your dating allegations,” Phainon said. “These are so funny. They said you’ve been secretly dating for years, based on one heatstroke interview right after you got back from Jarilo. Aventurine really outdid himself. It’s a freakin snowball out there, ‘Dei.”

Mydei looked at Phainon—really looked at him, and chuckled. “I’m glad you’re having fun out of that circus show, at least,” he said. His voice was heavy, like he could fall asleep anytime soon.

“Are you kidding? These are gold. I was in the middle of watching ‘The Moments Mydei and Robin crossed paths and gave each other references, when you came in,” Phainon laughed. He brushed his thumb under Mydei’s eyes. “How’s the recording? You look terribly exhausted.”

“Mmm,” Mydei hummed. “Anaxa kicked me out.”

Phainon furrowed his brows. He shut his phone and placed it on the table to give Mydei his full attention. “For a good reason, I suppose?”

“Mmm, I hadn’t slept a wink since yesterday,” Mydei said. “Finishing the last track of the EP. Anaxa came in this morning and just… kicked me out. Had Aglaea’s bodyguard escort me and shit.”

“Oh, dear,” Phainon frowned. “Why, did you decide that sleep is for the weak?”

Mydei scoffed. He did not say anything for a while, and with the quiet hum of his breath, Phainon would have mistaken him as sleeping.

But then, he opened his eyes and stared at Phainon.

“Veritas told us two days ago that while the EP was gold and could sell well, it still needs the punch for it to actually work,” Mydei said. “That man was fuckin insane, HKS. Crazy perfectionist, but I gotta admit. He knows his shit. This EP was intended as Robin’s coming-of-age experiment, and I attempted to preserve my mom’s legacy through her talent. This shit is so ambitious that they decided to name this Royalty. But it lacked something puchy. Not fit for a king or whatever. I don’t really understand what he was saying, but I kind of agree.”

Phainon combed Mydei’s wild mane, half-damp from sweat. “This Veritas is… Dr. Ratio, right?” he asked, trying to catch on.

“Yeah,” Mydei sighed. “Fucking Veritas Ratio. He had us in the studio for days, sunrise to sunset. Perdikkas was planning Veritas’ murder. We were all running out of creative juice, so in desperation, I pulled one of Mom’s samplers from way back. The one I never thought would see the light of day. Blow Me Away. You remember that?”

“Mm-hmm,” Phainon said, his hands now moved to Mydei’s temple, massaging it gently. Mydei sighed into his touch, and Phainon let out a smile. “It’s the song that your Mom wrote when she was pregnant with you? The one she envisioned to be your debut duet song, Mom and kid?”

“Mmm,” Mydei hummed, whether to answer Phainon’s question or as a response to his massage, Phainon would never know. “I was just taking a shot in the dark, not actually thinking it’s going to work. I just want to distract him. But then Veritas asked Robin and me to record it later that day. When it’s finished, I did everything I could to finish the demo as fast as I could.”

“And?”

Mydei smiled. “And… you listen to this.”

He pulled out his phone and played the song.

Robin’s harmonious scream was the first thing that Phainon listened to, followed by a series of explosive drums, riffs, and a harmony that was so powerful that Phainon couldn’t help but gape.

That song was the bomb. Robin’s voice came out so powerful. Explosive. She didn’t just match the energy—she met Mydei’s growl head-on with the same brevity. She wasn’t screaming—she was singing, every note sharp and alive, riding the rhythm instead of fighting it. They were truly a harmony— the prince and princess of their own domains, merging into one.

An absolute harmony.

Royalty.

The song ended with Mydei and Robin singing the last part of the chorus. The silence that crashed in after their final shout was chilling. Fiery. Full of energy. Phainon tried to describe it in his mind, but he couldn’t find the words. The energy still echoed in the walls of their room, filling it with a sense of soul.

“Damn,” Phainon said. “That’s amazing.”

“This girl, Phainon,” Mydei whispered. There’s softness in his tired gaze, admiration in his weary voice. “She could match Mom’s vocal range. That song was the toughest one to preserve. I couldn’t ever change it because it sounded too much like Mom. I didn’t want to erase any part of it. Yet, I could never sing it because I couldn’t sing her part. No one, not a single person, has ever met that range. And she just walked into that booth, and…”

Mydei paused. His brows furrowed, like he was trying to find the right word for it.

“And own it.”

“And own it,” Mydei repeated, closing his eyes again. His lips were tugged into a lazy smile.  “Yes, that’s it. That’s the word I’ve been looking for to picture her. Fuckin hell, she’s—I love you.”

Phainon paused. He did not know to whom the love was addressed; Robin? Gorgo’s image in Mydei’s head? Phainon? He could not tell when Mydei was slurry like that. Still, he brushed a finger on Mydei’s cheek and hummed, “Love you too.”

Mydei did not reply.

He had fallen asleep.

Phainon stared at Mydei’s peaceful slumber face, the ghost of a smile that remained from having his mother revived in the form of the melody. The contentment he felt made Phainon's heart flutter. He leaned to kiss Mydei’s

temple one last time before lying on the bed, falling to his much-needed sleep.

Mydei’s dreamy eyes were the last thing Phainon saw before he closed his own. And this time, somehow, despite having Mydei so close, Phainon dreams.

He stood in the shadows of the concert crowd, surrounded by faceless fans chanting Mydei’s name. Mydei was on the huge stage. He was bathed in the gold spotlight, voice soaring, hair whipping.

He was the star; everyone worshipped him, obsessed with him.

He’s perfect. A perfection that rules over the people.

Phainon raised his hand once, hoping for a glance, a smirk, a nod— something. But Mydei just looked forward. Never at Phainon, but at the lights, at something beyond the crowds that cheered for him.

He was looking at the stars, where he truly belonged.

A place where another face of the crowd like Phainon could never reach.

Chapter End Notes

Oooh the fear started to creep in. Please stay strong, Phainon!

Mydei nodded and was pulled back to whatever conversation that Aventurine had while Phainon walked outside the studio with Leonnius, snickering as he playfully punched his shoulder.

“You just want to escape that room after that thing with Gerald,” Leonnius called him on his bullshit as they got out of the room.

“Can you blame him? That’s awkward as hell,” Ptolemy laughed. “You never changed, huh, country boy?”

Phainon chuckled, grateful they were teasing him for his awkwardness, not his discomfort. He sat by the fence of the studio’s porch while the others complained about their packed schedules. As the breeze settled around them, Phainon started thinking maybe it was time to head home. The

listening party was over. Mydei had only invited him for that. Phainon didn’t need to stay for the rest of the day.

He stood, just about to head back in to excuse himself, when the studio door swung open. Mydei and Robin emerged from the door, which promptly brought a smile to Phainon’s lips. He was just about to greet them…

When he saw Robin’s shoes.

It’s Cherry Red Mary Jane—the exact same color as Mydei’s boots.

The boots that Phainon gifted him for Valentine’s Day years ago. The same color as the low-ankle boots he had at home, which Mydei had gifted him for White Day.

He pressed his lips and almost instantly realized what it meant.

“You’re uh… going to lunch together? For the paparazzi, I suppose?” he asked, deciding to shift his question into a safer territory.

“Yes, another paparazzi spotting,” Robin said brightly. “Mister Aventurine got me these just now, he said it’ll be good for the narrative if we match our shoes. Isn’t it cute?”

“It is,” Phainon said. He was smiling, but his mouth was dry, for some reason. “Cherry red looks totally cute on you. I bet the internet would eat it up.”

“Oh, they better,” Aventurine materialized like a smug genie from behind Mydei. “Because I’m placing a delightful little bet with Skott over these. I said: 'Get me one pair in this exact shade of red, and if I make it go viral and it sells out in under 24 hours, he owes me a million-credit contract.' If not?” He grinned. “I’ll pay for the shoes twenty times the market price. Sounds good, huh?”

Mydei sighed. “It’s for another teaser,” Mydei rolled his eyes, deciding to ignore Aventurine and pointing at the feather pendant hanging on his chain

necklace. “We’re going to get a hot dog at that popular spot by the beach. You want something? I could buy it for you.”

Of course you’re not invited, Phainon scolds himself mentally. It’s going to risk breaking the ruse if you do.

“No, it’s fine, ‘Dei, I’ll just go back home,” he said. “I need a nap, anyway. Still pretty exhausted from the long work week. I’ll see you soon, yeah?”

“Yeah, sure,” Mydei replied. A weak smile on his lips revealed that Phainon was a little disappointed. But without Mydei around, it would be hella awkward for him to be in this place. He would look even more out of place. “Take care. I’ll see you soon…”

…Love you, Phainon finished Mydei’s words silently in his mind. He only let out his biggest grin, waving Robin goodbye, and then walked to his car.

He should not have come to the studio. He should have stayed home, because then, in the privacy of their own home, they could part ways more properly. Phainon covered his mouth with his balled fingers, pressing his lips to his thumb and index fingers’ knuckles, mimicking the usual butterfly kisses he always gave Mydei before they parted ways.

He couldn’t even kiss Mydei goodbye now.

-

His drive back home was quiet, with only the occasional song from the radio playing. Phainon could feel his heart a little bit heavy, but he took a couple of deep breaths, reminding himself that this was a part of dating a celebrity. He knew what he was signing up for when he made the move to Mydei all those years ago. Mydei had always been kind enough to tell him everything about his job and to shield him from the media's negative aspects.

Mydei had always been so kind to him.

And Phainon should not be selfish. Not now. Not over damn shoes.

Why did he make a fuss about it, anyway? It shouldn’t matter that much. Phainon hadn’t even had a chance to wear those shoes these past months, so it wasn’t exactly their thing.

And besides, it’s just a ruse.

A story that Aventurine arranged to make some profit.

Robin wore it because it was part of the act. It was part of the music's advertising. Just like the pendant that Mydei wore. It was just symbolism to sell the narrative—the music.

The music that Mydei loved so much. The music that got him smiling like a little boy. The music that was his legacy, inherited by the mother who loved Mydei so much. The music that was his lifelong dream.

It was all just a big orchestra.

Nothing about it was true aside from their passion for the music they produced.

So it wasn’t supposed to be a big deal.

As Phainon parked his car in his apartment building, his phone rang suddenly, startling him. He grabbed it from the passenger seat… only to see Cyrene’s name on the screen.

Wait, Cyrene… called?

Now, his older sister was never one to call before texting first. Cy was never big on phone calls, even more so since he worked as a pilot, knowing there was a good chance her call couldn’t get through. For her to call without even a notice…

This might be an urgent matter.

Phainon quickly slid the button on his screen. “Hi, Cy,” he greeted.

“Hey, Phai,” she answered. Her voice was calm, almost too quiet. She paused for another second before she continued. “Uh, where are you?”

“Home,” Phainon replied. “I’m off duty today. But I just got back from driving Mydei to Anaxa’s studio. What’s up? Are you okay? Is Mom and Dad okay?”

“I’m okay. Mom and Dad’s fine too,” Cyrene said. “I just wanted to check on you. Are you okay?”

“Uh, yeah?” Phainon stared at the wall in front of him. “I’m fine.”

There was a beat of heavy silence, like Cyrene was thinking about something but deliberately chose not to say it out loud, as if she were waiting for Phainon to talk about it first.

Except that Phainon did not know what he was supposed to talk to her about.

“Cy? You there?”

“Phai,” Cyrene started, apparently not having the patience to gauge it from him now. “Is everything okay with you and Mydei?”

Phainon could feel his breath hitched.

Of course.

Of course, the news would reach her. Of course, she would ask about it.

And worst of all, Phainon did not know what to say about this whole fake-relationship thing. It was meant to make it look like Mydei and Robin were dating, and Phainon was told directly not to tell a single soul about it. Not even siblings, Aventurine had said. Phainon closed his eyes, mouthing curses to himself before he answered.

“Yeah, definitely,” Phainon said. “We’re good. He cooked me breakfast as usual. Like I said, I just drove him to the studio. Why do you ask?”

“Hmm, the studio,” Cyrene hummed. “He’s recording new songs?”

“Yeah, he has this upcoming collaboration with Robin. But you can’t tell anyone that, Cy. I think Mydei wanted to keep it a secret for now,” Phainon said. “They uh… they had been recording for the whole week, I guess? Mydei’s been so excited about it.”

“I see,” Cyrene said quietly. “But you two are doing well, right?”

“Totally,” Phainon answered, and Cyrene’s cryptic answer somehow made his chest feel even more pained. He bit his lower lip. “Why are you asking, Cyrene? Is there anything I should be worried about?”

“No, no, of course not,” Cyrene said. “It’s just… I’ve been watching CMZ, and I was wondering if you have something you haven’t told me yet.”

Phainon could feel his heart fall to his knees. Oh no, Cyrene and her perceptive eyes. Aventurine’s words about keeping the entire scenario from the outside party rang in his mind, making his heart pound faster. Phainon was thankful that this was not a video call. Cyrene would be able to call on his bullshit if it were.

“What? Nothing,” he chuckled. “Everything is okay in the Mydei-Phai household, I promise. Do you want the details of our makeout session, too?”

“Phainon!” Cyrene hissed. “You haven’t seen the latest news? The one that just got out now?”

“What? No! I’m driving. I don’t drive and scroll!” Phainon said. “What happened?”

“Mydei is with Robin, and…”

“And I know that! It’s not the first time Mydei has collaborated with a female singer. They’re probably just hanging out together as buddies.

Nothing to worry about.”

“They wear matching shoes,” Cyrene said, sounding impatient with Phainon’s dismissal. “Mydei was wearing your shoes. And he matched it with Robin. They call them a new pair. A couple. Do you know about this?”

Yes, he knew. And he had been sulking about it for the previous twenty minutes. But he couldn’t tell Cyrene that.

“Ah, it’s probably nothing,” Phainon said with a weak chuckle. “Robin’s stylist probably saw Mydei wear it one day and decided it would look good on her? It’s probably just a coincidence. It’s…”

“Phainon!” Cyrene said this more sternly this time. “They’re on a date! Take a look at the paparazzi photos I sent you just now! There’s no way nothing’s going on between them!”

Phainon sighed. He pressed the bridge of his nose with his fingers, feeling like he was going to combust.

“Cyrene, calm down,” he said. “We’re fine, okay? Nothing to worry about. If something’s going on between us, you’ll be the first to know. Don’t worry.”

There was another stretch of silence from the other side of the line. “Fine, if you say so,” Cyrene finally relented. “I’m glad to hear that. But if something does happen, please tell me, okay, Phai? You don’t have to go through it alone.”

“Sure,” Phainon said. “Thanks for checking up on me.”

“Anytime. And come home when you have time, okay, city boy? Mom said she misses you so much.”

Phainon could feel his lips curve into a smile. “I miss you guys so much, too.”

Cyrene hung up the phone, and Phainon had to take a couple more breaths before he could bring himself out of the car.

He idly scrolled through social media on his way to their shared penthouse and saw that #LionDove was trending. He pursed his lips, weighing whether he had to click on the tag, considering his feelings from this morning. Maybe he should just let it be. Maybe he should just distract himself with something instead.

But curiosity had taken the better of him.

He clicked the tag anyway.

The timeline was filled with Mydei and Robin’s photo at the hot dog joint near the Bastion Beach. Robin’s hair was tied into a high bun, and she was wearing an oversized red flannel, which Phainon did not know she had. She did not bring that when they said goodbye a few minutes ago. The stylist must have given the finishing touch on their way there. She was holding a corn dog, which, in one photo, she offered to Mydei.

In the other photo, Mydei bit the hot dog, and they laughed at each other as she wiped the sauce from the corner of his lips.

The caption of that particular photo, however, was what got Phainon.

@TimelyLionDove IN PRIVATE SHE’S WIPING THAT DAMN SAUCE WITH HER LIPS I JUST KNEW THAT. TRUST ME I AM THAT FEATHER PENDANT ON MYDEI’S NECK.

@mydeisguitarcase No please where do we get cherry red mary jane?? Hello???

@Gopherwilds was at the mall when i saw the image. People rushed to Dr. Markenz. Cherry red color sold out in golden hour don’t even bother coming.

@3amsimps It’s sold out online too T.T damn I was gonna buy a matching pair with my bf damn why people are moving so fast. T.T

@TimelyClockieDove they’re in love, Your Honor. And we’re so lucky to witness this.

@Nymphsss It’s the most beautiful hot dog date I’ve ever seen. I’m so glad they’re together, these photos cure my depression <3.

He took a deep breath as he entered his house and glanced at his shoe cabinet. His own pair of Cherry Red looked lonely there, just as he was now. He closed his eyes, taking another deep breath as he tried to recall Mydei’s face this morning when Blow Me Away played. His child-like joy, his brightest grin…

He smiled to himself.

If he could see those expressions on Mydei’s face again, it’s worth going through. He would endure this happily for months. Years. Lifetimes, if he must.

As long as he could keep seeing Mydei smiling like that, he would endure everything.

Even if he had to brave the loud noise of the whole world.

-

Chapter Summary

As the world falls in love with Robin and Mydei’s picture-perfect Dollywood Royalty Couple, Phainon wrestles with that strange, silly feeling in his chest

Chapter Notes

Happily.

Right.

Phainon had to focus on that part instead. Mydeimos Gorgo, the love of his life, the man who made mornings bearable, the person Phainon had always imagined spending the rest of his life with, was having a good time. He looked alive, radiant, and in his element. Robin Gopherwood, the celebrity Phainon had loved since middle school—the girl he had grown up watching on TV, whose music had filled Phainon’s teenage years, serving as a soundtrack to his best high school memories—was living her dream.

The two people Phainon cared about were having the time of their lives, a pivotal moment in their careers and their lives.

So he should be happy about that, rather than reading about the random noises people wrote about on social media, because they could only assume. They ate everything Aventurine was baiting them, nothing more. They knew nothing about Mydei or Robin.

Phainon knew everything.

So he should focus on what’s important: Their smiles, the fun they were having, the music they were making.

A pair of shoes was nothing in comparison.

Okay, now he could just have fun watching the campaign unfold, note down whatever crazy theories they came up with online, and recap them to laugh with Mydei later.

Yep. Sounds like a plan.

Phainon reheated the Pad Thai Mydei had bought him while humming a song from Robin’s latest album, then sat on the stool in the kitchen, scrolling through the hashtag as he ate. It continued to grow in volume, and not even just a typical fangirl scream in all caps or a keyboard smash this time. There were even complete analyses of their choice of wardrobe down to the smallest accessory, a few more fan edits on how “in love” they are, and there’s even a video of a woman who claimed to be a body language analyst, talking about how genuinely obsessed they are with each other.

Phainon scoffed. But out of curiosity, he played the video.

The woman looked mature. In her early thirties, if Phainon could guess. She wore platinum-framed glasses, red lipstick, and a well-tailored outfit that appeared to be designer. She looked legit. Like she knew what she was talking about.

“Now, watch this,” she said, tapping her screen to freeze a shot of Robin looking up at Mydei. “Robin’s eyes here look wide, soft, and unblinking. She’s not just happy; she’s invested. This is a young girl experiencing first love. And that open laugh. It’s nothing like Robin had ever done in public before.

Wow, okay. So there’s someone out there who spends the time to analyze a celebrity’s smile, after all. Good to know.

She then switched the screen to show a photo of Mydei.

“Now, Mydei might not be there yet. Like, maybe he likes her, but not quite in love. But he’s getting there. Because… look, what’s interesting about his gesture is… the shoulder shielding. The second he spots the paparazzi, his arm automatically comes around her. That’s a protective move. You can’t fake that instinct. This man cares about her.”

Yeah, of course he did. That’s what Mydei would do to Phainon, too, whenever he felt that Phainon was feeling uneasy. The kind of thing he did without thinking. Just purely from his genuine feeling.

No, wait a minute.

That wasn’t necessarily an act of love. That was Mydei caring for his coworkers, his bandmates, his fans—anyone. The analyst knew nothing about that. She was simply stringing together coincidence with confidence. Phainon scoffed, forcing the lump in his throat down with Pad Thai.

“Then we have the gravity lean. It’s subtle, but his torso angles toward her whenever she speaks. That’s admiration in motion. And finally, the smile… small, soft, gentle. That’s different from The Mydeimos’ Smile, which was

usually a cocky grin. That small smile was a genuine sign. The dawn of adoration. He’s starting to fall for her.”

Phainon could feel his lips curve into an amused smile.

Wrong.

That smile —the little curve, the gentleness in his golden honey eyes, that wasn’t adoration. That was Mydei looking at a Samoyed, or a story about a garbage can mascot.

Mydei’s real look of adoration was half-lidded golden eyes clouded in a mist of desire, face completely relaxed, but with his brows furrowed a little, like he couldn’t believe how he could even love.

The same look that he showed Phainon every morning when he woke up next to him. When he pressed against Phainon, making a show of last-minute resistance before he actually let Phainon go to work.

Yeah, none of them knew Mydei at all.

Phainon continued to watch the video. Now she was talking about the shoes; how Mydei’s were scuffed, while Robin’s pair looked new. She at least did her homework, saying that Cherry Red color had always been Mydei’s signature since his debut. He wore those shoes almost everywhere, and it’s likely that Robin's complete smittenness with him led her to match his aesthetic. Or, and this was a much higher possibility, that Mydei was giving it to her as a possessive sign.

Possessive sign.

Hah. At least she’s correct about one thing. Mydei was indeed a possessive man.

“Seems like you’re not as mysterious as you make yourself to be, ‘Dei,” Phainon hummed to himself, only half-amused because he was fixated with more images of his boyfriend staring at the pop stars with emojis

surrounding them, more theories, and then on a post that discussed why Robin / Mydei were not suitable for each other; clearly a Mydei-hater post.

Phainon found himself frowning when he realized that he lingered longer on these kinds of posts, feeling somewhat offended by how some people thought Mydei was not good enough for Robin, yet also confused about why he was rooting for his boyfriend to be with Robin.

He caught himself halfway through typing about why Mydei deserved Robin, realizing that he had almost gotten sucked into the stage that Aventurine set. Mydei was his. He wasn’t supposed to be Robin’s, and those haters’ posts were right. They were not a good match, because Mydei prefers men. Robin was just a fan of his work, and he did not have to defend Mydei and Robin’s relationship because it was not true.

He shook his head, scrapping his draft and moving on to the next post. But the more Phainon scrolled, the tag continued to grow as Phainon read into one thread that discussed why Robin/Mydei's relationship might fail, the tag increased into 1,000 new posts, 1,500, 3,000… 3,355…

Now, there were even more new trending words under the #LionDove tag. It’s the #CherryBombCouple, Dr. Markenz, Cherry Red.

Oh, by Kephale.

That acid in the pit of his stomach kicked back in.

Phainon groaned. He hated how the mention of the shoes still troubled him, despite his best efforts not to think about it.

Phainon put his phone down and closed his eyes, because he knew he should stop. He should steer clear of social media before it consumes him, because none of those were real. It was just Aventurine’s big circus. He knew that. He even knew that Aventurine would improvise along the way, adding a new twist based on the audience’s response online.

Except that he never thought that the improvisation that Aventurine created just touched something very personal to him.

Phainon wondered if Aventurine knew that.

Or Mydei… Did he even remember how much those shoes meant to Phainon?

We can’t always control the output, Mydei had warned him a week ago.

And Phainon had assured him that everything would be okay.

Well, it was okay.

He was just caught off guard, that’s all.

Right, well, again, it was just shoes. What they had now was far more meaningful than that. Heck, he could overwrite the meanings of those shoes! Maybe get a new matching pair in a different color, or even a whole new brand. He could give them to Mydei on their next special occasion. Perhaps the day he proposed. Or their wedding day. Phainon was Mydei’s real partner. He could easily propose something new to move past these sentimental knots.

It wasn’t a big deal. He could always overwrite it.

Phainon got up from his seat, deciding that since he no longer had the appetite for lunch, he might as well just distract himself by washing the dishes, doing his laundry, or cleaning the house. Anything to keep moving, because sitting with his thoughts proved to be counterproductive.

Still, despite constantly convincing himself that he was okay, the uncomfortable feeling stubbornly sat in the pit of his stomach, tugging his heart deeper with each passing second. He kept glancing at his shoe cabinet, staring at his own pair of Cherry Red shoes. Mydei gave them on White Day in the same year Phainon gave him the boots, and Phainon had teased him to no end, calling him for not being creative, et cetera, et cetera.

But Mydei said, in a flat, serious tone, that he gave him those pairs because he wanted something to match him; a fashion statement to mark them as a couple.

Phainon remembered how that answer had caught him so off-guard, his laugh stalling halfway as he was flustered terribly. Mydei had laughed then, kissing his “Phainon.exe stopped working” face to sober him up, and spent the rest of the week teasing Phainon about it.

But he wore the shoes all week, that bastard. Prompting Phainon to do the same, and got scolded by the airline for coming into work with that.

Phainon scoffed.

Yeah, a possessive man, indeed.

Phainon glanced at the shoes again. They were still clean and as good as new, not worn out or lived-in from use. He couldn’t wear them to work for obvious reasons, and he had so few occasions to wear them anywhere else. They rarely went out on their free days, deciding to spend what little time they had together in each other’s presence at home.

Maybe he should propose a vacation together somewhere, when Mydei’s summer tour ends.

Yeah, it’s been too long since they were out for vacation together.

His musings were interrupted by a ping of a message; the ringtone he reserved for Mydei. Phainon hesitantly opened the message, only to see a picture of a fluffy white cotton candy with a happy dog face staring back at him, with Robin’s cute duck face just next to it.

My Day Mouse <3 You and your favorite singer together.

Phainon snorted. He zoomed in on the picture, looking at how Robin’s face was a bit of a blur, while the cotton candy was crisp and crystal clear. It’s just so Mydei. He could be in the most beautiful place in the world, or be with the most beautiful woman who ever lived, and yet his focus would be on a damn cotton candy.

Phainon snapped a photo of the vacuum cleaner he just used to reply to Mydei’s message, but as he typed his text, Phainon paused to stare at the image.

It felt dull, somehow.

Boring.

So pale compared to Mydei’s life of Cherry-Red shoes, pastel-colored cotton candy, and the sparkling pop stars and Dollywood glamour surrounding him.

He discarded the picture and just sent the text instead.

You Close, but my favorite singer is still Mydeimos Gorgo ( ˘ ³˘)♥ Also, say hi to Robin for me. (Wow, so casually to The RobinTM. Cant believe this is my life now)

My Day Mouse <3 Fuckin dork. She said lets hangout smtm. G2g. Dnt forget to eat well. HKS.

You Take care. But Where is My kisses? (இ﹏இ`｡)

My Day Mouse <3 (  •◡•)╭∩╮♥ DO NOT reheat the Pad Thai it prob gone bad. Nvm u probably ate it alrd.

“Too bad you’re not here to stop me, Mydeimos,” Phainon said out loud to the hollow of his house, deciding not to type that because had Mydei known

that he indeed ate the Pad Thai, Phainon would never let him hear the end of it.

But Phainon let his smile linger.

Yeah, he was thinking too much about it.

Since he had nothing else to do around the house, Phainon decided to look for a new pair of shoes online, hoping to find something unique to buy for Mydei. New, unique colors or patterns. Something Mydei could use as his new signature.

However, anytime he types the keyword for “boots”, it’s always followed by Mydei and Robin's related words.

Boots Cherry Red, Boots Dr Markenz Mydei Robin, Boots and Mary Janes Robin, Boots and Loafers Cherry Red. Boots Couple Cherry Red.

Oh, by Kephale.

There’s no escaping them, isn’t there?

Phainon locked his phone out of frustration. But then, it rang again, signaling a new message.

Thankfully, it was Caelus this time.

Wait, why was he thankful that it was Caelus and not Mydei? Ugh, he must be more exhausted than he let on.

Partnurrr #2 (Cae) S.O.S, Snowy. S.O.S!!

Phainon furrowed his brows. He typed in a “hi!” but before he could type in anything, though, Caelus called him.

“Cae, he…”

“Snowy! Snowy! Are you free?” Caelus whispered. His voice sounded urgent, almost panicky. The use of Phainon’s childhood name alone alarmed him, making him sit straighter.

Caelus hadn’t called him that name since they both moved to Okhema.

“Yeah, I’m free. You okay, buddy?” Phainon replied, his voice thick with worry.

“Ok, great, can you come over?” Caelus whispered. “Danny boy is going insaaaaane!” he continued, with a long, dragged, scandalous voice.

“Danny… wh, Dan Heng? What happened? Why are you calling him Danny?” Phainon asked, getting up from his seat now because it sounded so serious. “I mean, sure, I can come over! Are you okay, though?”

“I’m okay, but…” Caelus hissed. “But please come if you can! This is Code S.”

Code S means Code Strange. Their old childhood signal for something weird is happening, and you need to get here now. Hearing Caelus use it for the first time in years made Phainon’s pulse spike. It’s either an extremely dangerous or abysmally stupid situation. With Caelus, those two categories often overlapped. But Phainon was curious, regardless.

“Alright, alright, I’ll be there soon,” Phainon said, before hanging up the phone. He quickly grabbed his jacket, slipped into his Cherry-Red shoes, and bolted out the door.

As he walked down the hall, he found it strange that he felt relieved to have something to do that was not house chores. Maybe it had something to do with the loneliness in his house, or the silence in his living room that was starting to feel louder than the trending tag ever could.

Or maybe it was just his imagination.

-

When Phainon entered Caelus’ house, he was faced by a dimly lit room, curtains almost entirely drawn, lamps partly turned on, and Caelus lying on the couch, a thin blanket draped over his body. There were empty bags of chips, chocolate wrappers, personal-size pizza boxes, and coffee cans around him.

It looked like a hedonistic catastrophe, which was weird, even for Caelus.

“Cae?” Phainon whispered as he slowly entered the house. “Caelus?”

Caelus’s head shot up, startling Phainon.

“Snowy!” Caelus jerked, rushing to grab Phainon’s shoulders. “You came!”

“Yeah, what happ—”

“Danny’s going insane,” Caelus whispered urgently. His eyes widened in horror. “He’s shutting us in for days! He won’t even allow me to open the curtain!”

Phainon’s brain racked with something to do, but then, an electronic whirring was heard, and the curtain was drawn up, letting in the bright golden evening sunlight. Caelus shrieked quietly, hiding behind Phainon when Dan Heng walked in from the kitchen, one hand holding a trash bag.

“Caelus, don’t rope Phainon into this,” Dan Heng deadpanned. He then turned to Phainon, his face looking apologetic, and Phainon instantly knew that this must fall into the ‘Abysmally Stupid’ category. “Thanks for coming, Phainon. But I am not going insane. It was all nothing but Caelus’s madness.”

“Our madness.”

“That was exclusively your idea. I was just playing along,” Dan Heng said, picking up the empty coffee can from the floor. “Apologize, now!”

“No, Danny boy, no. We shouldn’t break the immersion. Especially when we have a 3P that has just joined here!”

Phainon blinked, still trying to catch what kind of Caelus’ antics he had walked in on. His eyes swept over Caelus’ dramatic wide eyes, Dan Heng’s frown, and the snack carnage. “So this is a Code S for…”

Dan Heng glared at Caelus, which was welcomed by a defeated groan.

“Ugh, fine,” he said, letting his hands off Phainon’s shoulders and adjusting his position on the couch. “Sorry to shock you, Phainon. I’m helping Dan Heng with his method acting. Dan’s playing a gamer-stalker role in his next movie. So we came up with the idea to completely shut in to capture the true essence of isolation….”

“Your idea,” Dan Heng insisted.

“Is it always like this? Does Mydei always cook breakfast every morning?” Robin asked Phainon, when he finally sipped that hangover-cure drink (which he didn’t need), and Mydei finally stopped pestering him.

“He would die of starvation if I’m not,” Mydei was the one who answered. “That guy has a thing for unhealthy eating habits. I didn’t see the Pad Thai from yesterday. Did you throw it out like I said you should, or did you eat them?” he then asked Phainon, narrowing his eyes menacingly.

“Mydei likes to cook,” Phainon told Robin, ignoring Mydei’s question entirely. “He likes to feed people he loves and their mother. Like, seriously, he cooked for my parents once.”

“Aww,” Robin cooed dreamily, alternating his gaze from Phainon to Mydei. “May I ask how did you two get together? I… I mean, if it’s not too much to ask! If it intrudes, then…”

“Nah, it’s fine, Rob,” Mydei answered, finally taking off his apron and sitting next to Phainon, just in front of Robin. “It’s not that much of a story anyway, I was being a dick, giving Aglaea’s secretary attitude and shit, and HKS here really went all the way to scold me. Challenged me in a duel and stuff.”

Robin gaped, looking super invested in the story as she leaned forward. “Duel,” she murmured. “Like… a real duel?”

“Yeah, totally,” Phainon laughed, taking a bite of his salad before continuing. “Not so much, at first. Mydei invited me to his concert first and I dared myself to come in without his invitation. Then, after that, he challenged me at boxing, then a sprint, then another boxing session, and before we know it, uh…”

And they made out in the back of Mydei’s car, but Robin did not need to know that. It felt too private to share because, as kind, polite, and brilliant Robin was, she was not a friend.

Not yet.

She was barely an acquaintance. She was a person from the other side of the wall, slipping into the side where his sanctuary lies, where Phainon felt safest and was not ready to share with anyone just yet.

Not especially Robin.

“... and then somehow we kissed and Hyacine caught us, and she suddenly told us that she lost a bet. All this time, Aglaea and Anaxa had hosted a bet

on how long we would meet before we realized we wanted each other in that way.”

Phainon let out a smile, glancing at Mydei while his gut felt like it was pulled in four different directions.

But of course, Robin was Mydei’s friend. She was an important part of his life, now. Of course, he would tell her.

Phainon swallowed his salad. The taste of Aedes Elysiae, cooked by the man he loved most, now felt even a little bit… strange.

“Oh,” Robin laughed. “Madame Aglaea started it?”

“She won it,” Mydei said begrudgingly, shaking his head with the littlest scoff. “Cheated a little too, she kept egging me on to challenge HKS over and over again, so we could accelerate our progress, and she could win. If you ask Anaxagoras now, I think he would still hold a little grudge against her.”

And as the conversation rolled into a more casual chit-chat about their day, Phainon started to drift off into the other side of the glass wall again, watching Robin and Mydei go back and forth about the music, the schedule, about how they could bring a little bit of memorabilia of Queen Gorgo…

And Phainon couldn’t touch it. He could never be a part of that world. All he could do was smile with his mouth while his chest felt like a glass splintering from the inside.

So close, and yet so untouchable.

Phainon tried to squash those feelings away because like Mydei, Robin was just another Aventurine’s pawn. She did not actually like Mydei in that way, and had been respectful of Phainon and Mydei’s relationship until now.

And yet, Phainon felt a little bit like a stranger in his own house.

A third wheel in his own relationship.

That thought made him feel sick, because Phainon actually hated it. He hated that he felt jealous of something that wasn’t real, that he felt threatened by the ghost of what could never be. He hated the fact that he could never hold Mydei’s mom's legacy like Robin, to treasure it the way Mydei could only dream of all this time. That he locked away a massive potential from Mydei's life, because he came from a different side of the wall.

Because he would never understand how to unlock it.

The thought made him so sick that he could not even look Mydei in the eye.

Phainon excused himself to go to the shower, to which Robin replied with a wave of goodbye, a ‘see you again soon!’, and Mydei only grunted, his eyes lingering a little bit longer on Phainon before he got distracted with whatever celebrity stuff Robin spoke that Phainon could never hope to understand.

But Phainon did not go to shower. He sat on the bed instead, his finger scrolled past his work schedule idly as he stared at the smudge of his own body on the windowpane, the outline of last night’s desperation. He should wipe it away before the cleaners come to save himself the shame, but he couldn’t bring himself to move.

The door to their room opened, jolting Phainon from his daydream, and Mydei slipped inside their room.

“Hey, I’m going in ten minutes,” he said.

Phainon hummed, forcing a tug of a smile. “Here for your goodbye kisses?”

Mydei did not answer. He stared down at Phainon, his jaws clenched, and his eyes narrowed in a way that he was bracing for something, and—

Oh, that can’t be good.

Phainon shifted, but before he could get up from bed, Mydei sat next to him, holding Phainon by the thigh to keep him from moving.

“Don’t bother,” he said. “I know you’re not going to shower. You never shower in the morning if you’ve taken a bath the night before.”

Phainon gaped. He tried to open his mouth, but Mydei did not let him.

“You also don’t drink the night before work, no matter what time you fly the next day. You don’t dip into the jacuzzi without waiting for me. You don’t dream, Phainon. You never dream, much less talk in your sleep. And you never cried when you fuck me. And you always finish your breakfast.”

Mydei’s fingers gripped a handful of Phainon’s boxers as his golden eyes hardened into a glare.

“Do you really think I wouldn’t notice how uneasy you are?” he asked. “Do you really plan to send me away without saying anything? Do you think I’m that dumb?”

Phainon let out a sigh. “Mydei, you know I’m fine, I’m just…”

“No, don’t fuck around and give me a half-assed answer that ‘I’m fine’ because I fucking know you’re not,” Mydei hissed. The grip on Phaionon’s thigh tightened a little, and his gaze hardened.

Mydei looked furious, no, desperate, no…

He looked so restless.

Phainon pressed his lips, idly entwining his fingers on Mydei’s, and even though he knew he had to answer, the truth lay heavy on his tongue. It felt silly to even talk about his insecurities when Mydei’s here, caring about him and paying attention to Phainon’s discomforts, because he knew that it was all nothing but a product of his own mind.

“I’m sorry, ‘Dei,” he said quietly. “It was just… I just… I think I was just caught off guard by that shoes trend you got with Robin,” he continued. “I mean, I know it’s just a pair of shoes, and it’s stupid, I should have muted it and moved on with my life, but—”

Mydei gripped Phainon’s hand, muttering a Kremnoan curse under his breath. “Phainon Khaslana, I swear to Nikador’s wrath,” Mydei groaned. “I only allowed it because I think you were okay with it. You didn’t say anything, back in the studio. You were encouraging Robin! How would I know that you’re not okay with it? I thought you even forgot about the shoes. You never wear them anymore.”

“I don’t get any chance wearing them anywhere, work was crazy,” Phainon said. “When we do have free time, we always stay at home or work out at the gym. I couldn’t wear it either way.”

Mydei sighed, looking absolutely dejected and guilty. He cursed in Kremnoan once again.

“You were there yesterday! Why didn’t you say anything? Didn’t I say that you should tell me for every smallest thing you were uncomfortable of?”

“Because it is okay!” Phainon hissed, afraid that Robin would be able to hear it. “Like I said, I was just caught off guard because it went viral, and for a while, I think I’m sad that the shoe thing wasn’t ours anymore. But I’m fine now, it’s fine. I’m over it, I promise!”

Mydei shook his head, looking disappointed, and it made Phainon’s heart clench. A string of apologies was already heavy on his tongue, but then Mydei pulled his phone from his pocket.

“That’s it, I’m calling shit off,” he said. “The contract’s over. I’m not allowing Aventurine to do…”

“‘Dei, fuck, come on, are you crazy?” Phainon snatched Mydei’s phone, but Mydei gripped it tight, not allowing Phainon to take it. “The campaign has already launched. They already sold out the shoes everywhere! Aventurine probably got the contract. You can’t just cancel it, you…”

“Yes, I can,” Mydei interrupted him. “I can, and I will shut that down. Because I mean it when I said that I will stop the moment you feel uncomfortable, HKS. Because something like this is what I was talking about when I asked you to tell me what you feel throughout the campaign.”

“But it’s done anyway, so what’s the point? You will only get people in trouble!”

“Fuck people, Phainon,” Mydei said, his voice raised a bar, and Phainon flinched. He pressed his forefinger in front of his lips, asking Mydei to tone it down lest Robin hear them.

Mydei closed his eyes, took a deep breath, and held both of Phainon’s shoulders, as if trying to ground himself. “Seriously. Fuck people. Stop thinking about them for once, HKS. Fuck people. Fuck everything. I said that once, and I’ll repeat it now. The music, the legacy, they’re not more important for me than you.”

Phainon could feel his heart clenched.

“I know, I heard you. But the music is important for me, too, ‘Dei,” Phainon said, cupping Mydei’s jaws to calm him down. “Your music, your mom’s legacy. Those are the things that make you happy. That’s the things that make you who you are. They’ve been there before I met you. And I saw how it makes you feel. I saw how alive you become with that music, and I want that for you. It’s absolutely important for me that you get to have those moments, a chance to bring your Mom’s works to life. To grow as a musician while respecting your legacy. So please, don’t ruin it just because I’m being a little bit silly one day, okay?”

Mydei stared at Phainon, like, looking right into his eyes, as if he was searching for something. There was a little spark of pain there, and fear, and Kephale knows what else. Mydei then shook his head. He closed his eyes, as if trying to squash those thoughts away from his mind.

“But what about me?” he asked. “I want to respect you in the same way, too. Making sure you feel the safest with me. It’s absolutely important for me that you take such discomfort seriously and not brush it off as silly, Phainon. I want to spare you from that burden. What are we gonna do about that?”

Phainon sighed, a little chuckle on his lips. Of course, Mydei would challenge him for that, too.

“We’re going to treat it as a first warning, then,” he said. “A warning for me not to take it lightly again, and not doom-scrolling on Aventurine’s circus again.”

“And a warning for me to double-check if you’re okay with Aventurine’s plan?” Mydei offered. “Even if you said you’re fine.”

“I’m always fine with it,” Phainon huffed. “It was just because that particular improvisation actually touched our personal stuff that it caught me off guard.”

“Mmm,” Mydei hummed. “That’s not good enough.”

“What’s not good enough?”

“I want to make sure you feel absolutely safe and comfortable with everything,” he said. “But you always ignore your feelings. You always think about other people, and I can’t always ask you and look at your eyes and tell if you’re being too generous. I need something to help us with that. Like… um…”

“… A quiet signal,” Phainon said quietly, his mind wandered back to Dan Heng’s advice.

“Hm?” Mydei asked. “Quiet signal?”

Phainon told him about Dan Heng and Caelus’ discreet way of communicating during promotions. To his surprise, Mydei listened intently, chin propped on his hand, humming at all the right moments. When Phainon finished, Mydei suddenly rose, rummaged through one of Phainon’s drawers, and came back kneeling in front of him. He set something gently into Phainon’s palm.

It was his choker. The double-band choker Phainon had always used when they were first dating. The one that Mydei always liked to tug at when he kissed him roughly.

“Put it on me,” Mydei said. His tone left no room for protest.

Phainon blinked, startled. “What?”

“You heard me,” Mydei said. “Put it on me, HKS. This way, whenever you see a picture of me, you will always remember who I belong to. I will make sure this stays off Aventurine’s list. No merchandise based on this, no matching gimmicks. This is mine. Ours. A quiet symbol that I belong to you.”

Phainon’s throat went dry. “You’d wear it? All the time?” he asked. “Will… Aventurine… allow it?”

“He will,” Mydei said confidently, his voice was so stern it was almost a growl. “Now, please.”

Phainon’s fingers trembled at first, but he steadied them with a quiet breath as he fastened the clasp. The leather sat snug around Mydei’s throat, stark black against his pale skin, sharp as ink across parchment. For a moment, Phainon just looked at him, heart hammering. He had worn this choker countless times himself, but seeing it on Mydei—his Mydei, shifted something inside him. It wasn’t just an accessory. It was a vow. A quiet signal only they understood.

When Phainon’s hands lingered there, Mydei caught them, kissed his knuckles, then pressed them against his chest.

“Now,” Mydei said. His golden eyes were wild, like a forest fire. “Do you like it, fos mou?”

Phainon’s heart squeezed. “Yeah,” he stammered. “You’re… uh, amazing. Always.”

Mydei’s mischievous smile was back. “Mmm I’m sure you like it. Your little friend there seemed excited, too,” he said, patting Phainon’s groin. "Please give him my regards. This is all I could do for him until we meet again.”

He kissed Phainon’s right hand, then parted his lips, dragging his tongue in a slow, deliberate line from the base of Phainon’s palm to the tip of his

thumb. A playful bite lingered there, like an eager little cat asking to play, before he finally let go.

Mydei then got up to his feet, chuckling. “Safe flight, Phainon.exe,” he whispered, brushing kisses over his nose, his cheeks, his jaw. “Call me when you land.”

Phainon could only nod, still dazed, still trembling. When Mydei left, the silence was thunderous, but it was gladly welcomed, this time.

When he came back from the haze of Mydei’s departure, Phainon realized he was flushed, half-hard, and undone simply from fastening a clasp around Mydei’s neck.

Maybe they would have to unpack this—Phainon’s sudden obsession with his accessories on Mydei, and that new goodbye Mydei just did, and the sexy implication that goes with it.

Yep, he would do that. But not today.

Today, Phainon decided he could let go of his unnecessary fears. Because now, more than ever, he believed they would be fine.

He needed to clean up and get ready for work, too.

…Well, right after he handled a far more urgent matter in his pants.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Ghosts
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Phainon finally understand the weight of his decision; the ghosts that come along with the fame that he pushed Mydei to.

Chapter Notes

Hi hello! It's me again with... the angst I didn't even see coming? T.T I feel like I must apology in advance. But this is a chapter where everything got worse (before it gets better! This is an angst with happy ending after all)

also this was beta-ed by very kind Norii from X! thank you for dealing with my ramblings and annoying self-doubts!

The week’s flying schedule was brutal.

Phainon always hated both ultra-long-haul and multiple short legs, but if he had to choose, he would rather choose the former in a heartbeat.

Because multiple short legs always consist of a blur of airport-briefing-cockpit-report with so few breaks in between, like a marathon that he must finish on his own. The layover cities were often reduced to airport highways and hotel rooms.

His favorite joke about running short legs was comparing it to being thrown into a hamster wheel and being forced to run as fast as possible. He could only focus on putting his foot in front of the other, keeping the wheel spinning while the world blurred around him.

Except when he stepped out of the wheel, nothing was the same anymore.

Phainon only realized it when he flew the last flight before his mandatory rest. He was supervising the descent into Styxia Airport when Plionis, his First Officer, hummed a melody that he knew too well.

Goddess. Robin and Mydei’s song. There’s no denying it.

“Catchy,” Phainon commented off-handedly. “What song is it?”

“Oh, it’s Goddess, Robin’s new song with her new boyfriend,” he replied. “Out only yesterday.”

Wow, two punches in a single breath. Boyfriend. Yesterday. Phainon didn’t even know that the first song was already released. He really lost track of time with all the back-to-back flights.

Mydei must have forgotten to mention it, too.

He must have forgotten that his song’s release date had always been important for Phainon. He liked to see the first twenty-four hours of Mydei’s song perform on the chart, watching as the number crawled up. Mydei called him out one time, saying that it was a bad habit. He didn’t really care how his song performed on the chart, and Phainon shouldn’t either.

But Phainon did anyway, brushing Mydei’s protest off with a tease about him sucking at math and numbers in general.

His lips curved into a smile, thin and tired. He’d check the charts later. Now, he gotta land the plane first.

“Alright, hummer, you want to call tower for clearance now, or should I do that while you hum to the next chorus?” he asked, teasing the now flustered rookie. Plionis stuttered to answer him that yes, he’d contacted the tower, and while the aircraft descended, Phainon couldn’t help but wonder how tough the past few days had been for Mydei.

The release of a new song and album usually meant a really tight schedule for him. It must be even worse with Aventurine’s crazy timeline as they

tried to sell the Summer Tour tickets. It must be a cycle of shooting - studio - promotions - interviews for him; the same hamster wheel that Phainon endured too, only that Mydei’s wheel is a more glamorous one, filled with limelights and cameras.

This was always the toughest part of their relationships; with their communication reduced to voice notes and short messages, only enough for sweet dreams, close-up selfies showing each other’s exhaustion, and very rarely, brief recaps of their days. And between the exhaustion, white noise, and the choppy signals, Mydei often fell asleep on the phone as soon as his head hit the pillow.

It’s crazy how fast the world outside of his flight plan moved.

As the plane made the final part of taxiing to the gate, Phainon wondered what it would be like if one of them had chosen a different career path. Maybe if he had accepted Aglaea’s offer to model for her men’s clothing line, his life would have turned out differently. He might have been in the same industry as Mydei, orbiting closer, crossing paths more often. He could have understood Mydei better, perhaps even offered genuine input on his marketing or artistry, instead of just cheering him on from the sidelines.

Or maybe, and this was a very strange thought to think about, if Mydei had pursued culinary instead of music, perhaps he could be home more often. Phainon could come home to Mydei in an apron; he would have a more regular schedule, and his biggest challenge would be a flirty coworker smitten over how perfectly he could roast a Peking duck.

The mental image made Phainon scoff at himself.

Stupid.

There’s no way it could ever happen. Mydei always loved music. It was literally running in his veins, with both his parents being musicians. And Phainon couldn’t imagine being anything other than a pilot. He loved flying and keeping people safe and comfortable as they flew across the world with him. It was always his dream since he was a little boy.

He didn’t know where those thoughts even came from. They had made it clear from the start of their relationship that neither of them should change careers or anything about each other. They would make it work somehow.

Phainon could still remember his first proposal to move in together after they had dated for several months.

“I mean, it doesn’t have to be now, now. But I’m always game if you do, Mydei,” Phainon said, feeling utterly nervous in the face of Mydei’s poker face. “Time, distance, they’re trivial compared to my love for you. I will always try to make it work with you. But being in the same house does have its benefits, right? I can kiss you goodbye before you go, I can keep the house clean for you, and I can snuggle you. I can give you the world!”

Mydei snickered. His stoic face was cracking into a cheeky smile. “You’ll hate me the first months I don’t come home from tour,” Mydei teased. “You’re a horny freak. You’re gonna fuck someone else in my own house in the third week I don’t come home.”

“I will NOT!” Phainon shot back, brows furrowed in genuine offense. “I’m only a horny freak when it’s you! And I swear I’ll be the best boyfriend ever. Besides, yearning is part of the game, y’know? It spices things up. We’re gonna have the kinkiest phone sex and the hottest one whenever we’re reunited.”

And they did. For four years, they had built a rhythm that worked, filling every corner of the house with their presence, carving their own sanctuary on weekends, loving each other even in their absence. So really, nothing changed—nothing was out of the ordinary.

So why was he even thinking about it?

Phainon must have been more exhausted than he thought, and maybe he missed Mydei more than he actually let on.

When the plane finally landed, Phainon quickly grabbed his phone and called Mydei. Sadly, it went straight to voicemail. Mydei must be somewhere he couldn’t use his phone. Maybe a radio interview, or perhaps

he’s in the middle of a shoot. Phainon lost track of his schedule, barely keeping up with his own, due to the madness of it all.

But he did not have to wait long to hear Mydei’s voice, because as soon as Phainon stepped out of the aircraft, Mydei’s voice was everywhere.

It poured from a portable speaker slung at a teenager’s hip as she skipped through the terminal, singing along with Robin’s oooh lalala. It floated from the duty-free shop, blasting over racks of perfume. It bled through the waiting room TVs, synced with glossy commercials. And along his walk to the cab station, Phainon saw Cherry Red shoes everywhere; worn by a trendy couple who took selfies, by a group of girls, another couple…

And as he got into a cab to his layover hotel, the taxi radio also played that song. Mydei’s voice was rougher in the poor-quality signal and the half-assed stereo.

And when his taxi slid past the city center, there he was—Mydei, ten stories tall, blazing across the largest LED billboard in the square, illuminating the night city streets with the red and golden light from his image.

The Royalty is Throned Get Ruled This Summer Pre-Order Now

After the text, another photo popped up. This time, it was Mydei with Robin.

Oh, it’s the album art of the EP.

Phainon gazed at the image. The background was bold red, Mydei’s kind of Red, and he was sitting in a crystal throne in the color of blood—the same throne that was seen in Queen Gorgo’s last album before she went on hiatus. His white shirt, accented in gold, hung half-open, revealing the chest tattoo, paired with black leather pants and Arcadia boots. His hair was loose and messy, his hand balancing a golden glass like a king in the middle of his coronation.

And then there was Robin. Perched sideways on his lap, her black-booted feet dangling from the throne’s arm, her swan-fur dress glittering under diamond shoulder pieces. Fingerless gloves framed her hands as they hovered above Mydei’s cheeks, tilting a crown above his head. His own fingers, just barely visible behind her, held a tiara over her updo hair as if to complete the picture. Together, they looked straight into the camera, their blue and golden eyes fierce and untouchable, like royalty from Dollywood, daring the world to challenge them.

And on Mydei’s lips, there was that smug tug of a smile he only wore when he was winning.

Royalties.

Phainon could feel his chest constrict at how crazy incredible that album art looked.

He had seen it before, of course. Mydei had sent him the raw results of the photoshoot, as well as behind-the-scenes images. He had known all about it since that first creative meeting in one of Aventurine’s mood boards. He knew what every color represented, what every gesture meant, what Aventurine’s team hoped the audience would read.

Yet, it still stunned him how… real the actual execution was.

It was polished to perfection, every hue and contrast sharpened into meaning, every expression sharpened into narrative; the glamour they tried to convey, the burning, rebellious passion of two young musical royals shared in the five songs of the EP.

It was meant to sell the idea that they’re so good together.

And Phainon was sold.

Had he not known about it, he would have thought they were actually together, and Phainon would have rooted for them because, aesthetically, they were flawless. Golden to silver, black to white, red to lavender—a

pairing so seamlessly woven together it had no room for any other color— for any other person.

And they’re perfect for each other, too, in a prolific way that Mydei was the prince of rock and Robin was the princess of pop.

He knew, yet it did not stop him from being struck by the polished final image.

Seeing Mydei live into that role with Robin, sitting on a symbolic throne that once belonged to his mother, Phainon felt as if Mydei were a different man entirely. Like this couldn’t be the same Mydei that curled into his embrace in the morning, hissing like a spoiled little cat at the threat of a cold shower.

He looked so surreal, in the same way the stars were surreal for Phainon; he could see them, but could never fly high enough to reach them.

He could, technically. However, that opportunity had passed many years ago. If Phainon were a model, maybe he could’ve made it into the album art. The music video. Up there in Mydei’s world, if only as a dim background light.

No, bad thought, Phainon, no.

Even if you are a model, you can’t always be with Mydei.

You know what you’re dealing with, dating a rock star. There’s always part of him that belongs to the rest of the world. You can’t always have all of him for yourself.

He stared at the digital billboard one last time. Somehow, looking into Mydei’s pixelated eyes on the LED screen made it feel like all their years together had been nothing more than a vivid dream—no more real than the kind Nereia might have. No more real than an average fan’s fantasy.

Phainon was so close to being swallowed whole by that thought, if not for the fact that Mydei was wearing a choker in that album art.

His choker.

Remember who I belong to.

Phainon’s breath caught, then escaped in a shaky scoff, feeling relieved in a way he almost fell to a cliff in a dream and jolted awake from the sensation.

Yeah, don’t fall for it, Phainon. He’s still the same Mydei. This couldn’t be any more different than any of Mydei’s promotional albums; just a spectacle.

Oh, Kephale, he’s so, so exhausted.

He couldn’t wait to get to a proper bed and sleep.

“That Gorgo boy finally does something good, huh?” the taxi driver suddenly murmured, distracting Phainon from his own thoughts.

Phainon raised his brows. “Hm?”

“Yeah, the Gorgo boy,” he said, nudging at the Radio playing the song. “He’s been musically stagnant these past few years. Good songs, no actual fire. Almost sounds like a sellout. This song is the first time he actually broke through. Guess all he needed was a talented woman backing him up, huh.”

Phainon did not react. He did not know what to say or think, but he felt the sting he could not describe flicking at the edge of his exhausted mind.

Ouch.

“I don’t know, I kind of like him,” Phainon said, quietly thanking Kephale that he was far too spent to strangle an unsuspecting old man. “His music is so good, and people love it. Even Robin herself. His band is one of the most popular rock bands in the world, too, isn’t it?”

“True, but popular doesn’t mean good,” the old man insisted. “You’d understand if you listened to Gregoria Gorgo’s original material. She was the real talent. A total hit. Too bad she got knocked up so early. I had high

hopes for her son, but—” the old man tsked. “He was so uninspired until they paired him with a good woman. They even brought back one of Queen Gorgo’s songs on the radio with that release! Do you know how rare it is for a twenty-year-old song to get airtime outside the Nostalgic Segment? He finally makes his mama proud.”

Phainon did not know what to say to that. He was too exhausted to think, or to be offended, or even to fake a laugh. He only hummed, deciding that agreeing is far easier than arguing.

Can’t even defend your man in front of a stranger, his mind shouted. Best boyfriend that ever lived, my ass.

The old man seemed to be more interested in rambling than having an actual conversation, because even without Phainon saying anything more substantial than a hum, he went on to talk about Queen Gorgo in her prime, and how Robin brought back her spirit with Mydei supporting her. He also mentioned that Mydei often looked inspired when collaborating with female singers, including Misia.
