The same bombastic charm, the same rockstar edge—I don’t even know what they expect anymore. I was chased by the thoughts that I owed her my music, my life, and the only way I could pay it was by carrying her legacy. So I did just that, hoping that someday I’ll get it right. People will get the closure, and I’ll deliver my duty. Maybe then, I will finally be free. But I can never live up to her. I couldn’t even finish half the songs she left behind. Maybe I could, if I’d been born a woman. But it’s just… not me.”

Mydei clenched his fists, his shoulders visibly shaking. Phainon instinctively reached for Mydei again, but he held it back.

“‘Dei…”

“When I heard Robin’s demo songs, when I saw her in the recording booth, I found clarity. All this time, I have always fallen short because I am not a woman. And Robin is a woman, so I put two and two together and thought that maybe it didn’t have to be me, specifically. I think it makes more sense for a woman to carry another woman’s legacy. So I talked to Robin about it, and she was hesitant. Not because she thinks that she couldn't do it, but if

she were to take Mom away from me. Heh. Like I didn’t spend my whole life trying to get out of her shadow.”

Mydei scoffed. He let out a dry laugh at a humor that only he could understand. But there was a tear dropping from his eyes.

“So I began to relate her to Mom every chance I get. It was a fair deal between us. Rob got to rock and get out of her Clockie Princess persona, and I got to be away from Mom’s name. The ruse was maintained strongly. It sounded like a win, except I didn’t think that you could perceive it differently. I guess I was too desperate to be free.”

Mydei let out a little sob now, so quiet that Phainon could barely hear it. He wondered how many times Mydei had done this, crying quietly to himself so no one would hear.

“But ‘Dei, that’s not your fault,” Phainon said. “I also lied to you, insisting that I’m okay.”

Mydei let out a humorless laugh. “Oh, please, I was being hypocritical too,” he said. “I was mad at you for lying to me, while I’m doing it myself. I kept you in the dark about how cowardly I am because I don’t want you to think I’m an ungrateful bastard. Because you seemed to think highly of my Mom, too. I was afraid that the reason you like me is partly that I am my mother’s son.”

“You think I’d ever do that to you?” Phainon asked, voice breaking.

Mydei smiled sadly. “I don’t know. But I didn’t want to take my chances. What you think of me is very important to me.”

Mydei’s voice was small, almost sulky, like a child who had just admitted that he stole the last piece of the cake.

That broke Phainon’s heart.

“You know,” Phainon said softly, “the reason I was so insistent… was because you were glowing when you were singing with her. That time in

the studio, that time when you two were talking, I thought you were happy. I thought you were proud to finally release her work that had been dusting in the corner. I thought that you were looking so joyful, in a way that I had never seen before… and I never did that to you. We dated for four years, and I could never help you the way Robin could. So I think… I think my presence only held you down.”

Mydei shook his head. “I guess that’s my fault, too, for never showing you expressions during our time together. You might never guess, but I’m happiest when I’m with you, Phainon,” he said. “I mean, don’t get me wrong. You were right about the collab, it made me happy. I did. I was so overjoyed. Because, despite everything, I love Mom. I love her music. As heavy as her legacy was on my shoulders, I also love carrying it for her. But I was mostly happy to see my way out of her shadow. But when the PR stunt chipped away at what we had, and you started mentioning her, I thought What if I made a mistake? What if this plan I had to get out of her shadow would make you love me less? Maybe part of the reason you dated me was that I am a son of Gorgo. And if I let go of her name…”

“Dude, stop,” Phainon hissed. “I am more of a folk guy, remember? I didn’t even know about your mom before I dated you.”

Mydei shook his head. “Yeah, folk guy, whatever. But I can’t help that thought eat me alive. It’s been repeated enough times since I was a child.”

Phainon pressed his lips. “Fair point,” he said. “Then it’s my fault, too, for not making my feelings clear. I never admitted to you that I’m jealous of Robin. People said she had always had a crush on you. And the way you praise her, I thought you started to see that dating her would be better than dating a nobody like me.”

Mydei smiled again. “Robin always liked rock,” he said. “She told me that she’s been trapped in that Clockie Studio since she was five. They had a long contract for her. She had always wanted freedom to express her true passion. Some songs she wrote were from her early teenage years. The studio discarded it every time. Nobody in that gigantic company wanted to follow up on her passion project, afraid that she would flop and ruin her own name, until Aven stepped in with that PR stunt of his.”

Phainon raised his brows. “Aventurine?”

Mydei hummed. “The management only agreed to Robin Goes Rock if they got insurance. He proposed me as his insurance. He gambled on me and ended up setting both Robin and me free from our restraints.”

Phainon scoffed. So it was true, what Aventurine said. He always placed his bet in the right hands.

“But we sacrificed your feelings in the process,” Mydei added again.

Phainon shook his head. “I did that to myself. You’ve done more than enough to take care of me,” he said. “And honestly… I’m glad it happened. Without it, Robin wouldn’t get to chase the genre she loves, and you’d still be stuck under your mom’s shadow.”

Mydei’s eyes softened. “If I’d known losing you was the risk, I never would’ve agreed. That’s too high a price. You may be a person who could love someone enough to let go, but I’m not. “ I will not let go of a person when I have a choice to fight for them.” He let out a smile, then added, “Rob said the same. She was terrified her wish would hurt you. She wanted to be your friend, so it would be easier for you to see me with her. But… you’re always so starstruck when she’s around. She never knew what to do around you that wouldn’t make you feel awkward.”

Phainon laughed. “Yeah, I guess I am,” he said. “It’s so uncool.”

“Good thing I didn’t date you because you’re cool,” Mydei grinned, the teasing in his voice was back.

Phainon giggled, and for a while, silence filled the room, while Phainon was gazing at his hand, open and just a few tiny inches away from Mydei.

“The lipstick was her idea too, you know,” Mydei spoke again. “When… that happened on the stage, I threw a fit. Everyone left me alone, afraid of the tantrum-rockstar. But she was there, she stood with me even though I shot curses at her, cried with me, and she said apologies a million times. She was the one who came up with the idea to reverse the narrative. The

public always overwrote you. The shoes, the choker... She said maybe we should use the lipstick to kiss you. To show you that I don't let the public overwrite us again. To claim the story and make it ours. I was so desperate to make up to you that I went with her idea.”

Phainon blinked, stunned. He hadn’t thought Robin could be that considerate. He didn’t know that Robin would care so much about his feelings. He almost felt a little bit ashamed for thinking badly about her.

“And it was adorable,” Phainon said. “It should have worked, but by the time it happened, I was already consumed with the idea that you don’t want me anymore. You'd better be off with Robin.”

Mydei shrugged. “Maybe next time, we should talk about it instead. Just like what your mom said.”

“Agreed,” Phainon said. “I’m sorry I rejected you, ‘Dei. I’m sorry I didn’t come clean with what I feel. I’m sorry, I thought that I would lose you, and yet I didn’t put up any fight to keep our relationship. I should have told you very clearly how much I love you.”

That seemed to spark something inside Mydei. He blinked, looking surprised, but then he grinned.

“Then tell me now, Phainon,” he murmured, voice barely above a whisper. There was a flicker of fear in his eyes, like he needed to hear it again just to believe it. “Say that word again, and say it like you really mean it this time.”

“I love you,” Phainon said, closing the space between their hands on the table and placing his palm over Mydei’s, fingers intertwining. “I love you, ‘Dei. I love you, Honeycake. I love you, I love you so so much, I love you Kotik.”

“I love you too,” Mydei replied. “I love you so fucking much, you have no idea.”

“So work on that, you lazy little cat. Let me have the idea.”

“Fucking hell, you stupid dorky dog. Come here, then.”

Phainon leaned across the table to kiss him, and Mydei met him with enthusiasm. The chair scraped loudly on Phainon’s side as he shifted forward. It was an awkward angle, his neck strained too far—but he kissed him anyway. Gently. Passionately. Wholeheartedly.

Like he meant the whole world, this time.

Because that was the truth.

The pieces of his heart slid back into place like a puzzle, the cracks filled with gold, like kintsugi. Making the broken even more beautiful, shining, gleaming.

And as he breathed Mydei’s sigh, again, the sweet smell of him, the warmth of his skin, the smile that he showed as he stared at Phainon, he thought that, well, he wouldn’t mind walking through that hell again, or watching his sanctuary fall in ruins.

If it means that he’ll be here, in Mydei’s arms, where his real paradise lies.

Chapter End Notes

If you feel that they deserve more, indeed they do! I did thinking about writing a happier epilogue with Robin, Aven, and obviously, just with our boys, hence I added extra chapter.

Thank you again for reading. I hope you enjoyed it!

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Epilogue: Mydei
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

As he and Phainon reunited, Mydei reminisced about what had happened between him and Phainon, while moving forward to do better and love him better.

Chapter Notes

Ah finally the ending! My apologies for putting this off for so long. I joined Phaidei week and I got caught at work and... well, hehe, here we are. Again, I thank Noriko my best girl for listening to my ramble about this, for inspiring me with the pretty-nails stories, and with her love aaa thank you friend! this one is for you!

Oh, and I switched the POV to Mydei to explain some of the parts that I couldn't in Phainon's angle. I hope you enjoy it regardless!

Thank you again for reading, commenting, and leaving kudos up to this point. It is truly an honor for me >.<

It felt like a dream that was too good to be true.

Mydei was in Phainon’s parents’ house in Aedes Elysiae, cooking in Phainon's mom’s kitchen, wearing Cyrene’s apron, kissing Phainon…

Kissing Phainon.

This had felt so far out of reach a week ago: the silence, the distance, the fear lodged in his chest; the last time they’d seen each other, he’d walked out, feeling betrayed and unloved—and Phainon hadn’t done anything to stop him.

This felt like a dream, still, when he was getting used to the hollow clawing at him so persistently that he almost felt like he had lost his heart altogether.

This felt too much like a paradise.

Perhaps he had a car crash on his way to Aedes Elysiae, and he was dead, and this was the heaven that the holier men promised. Maybe this wasn’t Phainon at all but an angel wearing his face…

… until Phainon bumped their noses and umph’d into his mouth.

Mydei smiled into the kiss.

Yeah, no. Angels couldn’t be this awkward.

This was definitely his Phainon.

Mydei wanted to put away the table that kept them apart to kiss him until sundown, to embrace him, to cling to him till the morning comes to make up for the time they drifted apart for the past three weeks, but they were in Audata’s kitchen. Any of Phainon’s parents (and Cyrene!) could walk in any moment, and a literal big dog was huffing around Mydei’s ankles, campaigning for seconds. He broke the kiss, told Phainon to finish lunch, and fed Big Snowy.

This felt like a movie flashback, where Mydei tended to Phainon’s pet while Phainon was eating his food, staring at him with that puppy-like excitement in his eyes and a smile that could put the sun to shame.

But he was here, it was all real, and he got to have this moment again; the countryside nostalgic feeling he never had, the small loving family he never got to experience, and a simple moment of domesticity with a man whom he loved and loved him in return, despite all the insecurities, misunderstandings, and the unspoken truth between them.

The man who had given him a home, when Mydei never dared to dream of a place to belong.

Mydei still couldn’t believe how Cyrene contacted him yesterday, when he was just finishing the rehearsal for the concert on the weekend. She texted him urgent!!!!!!!!!! with that many exclamation marks, and Mydei was scared that it was about Phainon, that maybe Phainon finally found someone else. Someone who was less complicated than Mydei, whose whole life wasn’t a preloaded shell filled by his dead mother’s legacy, and…

Mydei shook his head, considering what Ratio told him about “keeping your mind from wandering too far”, and picked up his phone to call Cyrene.

She told him everything.

Phainon’s angle, Audata’s advice, and everything in between, uncensored— including Mydei’s mistakes (Cyrene, Mydei learned, had no qualms about talking shit to his face) and, of course, Phainon’s shortcomings.

You two are in the wrong, if I’m gonna be honest, she said calmly, like she was just listing groceries instead of stripping Mydei of his flaws. You can’t just quietly go out and keep him in the dark about what you do in the name of protection. Because sure, you could protect him from the external factors, but you’re ignoring the demons in his mind that could thrive from him not knowing.

And he loves you, Mydei. But we both know he’s just a dumbass. He thought you had found the better love there in the Dollywood spotlight where he couldn’t be. He knew it was a ruse, but he couldn’t help but think that he held you back. That he would never understand your world, and so he removed himself from the picture…

“He thought a lot of things, but he never asked a single thing,” Mydei had said then.

Because Mydei knew that it wasn’t true at all, if Phainon asked him, Mydei would confidently say that he would never find a better love in Dollywood. Sure, they exchange the word love so easily, so expressively, but it was all different kinds of love altogether; it was mostly a play pretend, an off-hand remark to admire someone’s art, the person they presented, the fame they

earned, but rarely the man within. Strip Mydei of everything he owned; his name, his fame, his music, and no one will ever look at him twice.

And he was confident to say that because he had stepped into the spotlight since he was very young. He had witnessed the industry for over a decade, and never had he ever seen real love formed in Dollywood. It was always an exchange of benefits, mostly. His parents were proof enough. But it was not a surprise at all, once you got there. What do you expect from a world that weaponizes feelings into profits and marketable jargon?

Still, Mydei told Cyrene that he wasn’t mad at Phainon. He admitted his own mistake, too. He had been in the industry so long that he had forgotten that not everyone could see the inside as clearly as he did. Phainon most likely couldn’t differentiate the thin line between admiration, lust, and love in the Dollywood language. Because for him, it was love all the same. No motives, no ruse. Sure, Mydei had assured him to make it absolutely clear to Phainon what to expect in the PR stunt he approved to include Mydei in, including the unexpected. But he should have always assumed that Phainon didn’t know.

Because he didn’t, and they should have known better not to let the silence stretch because Phainon would always rather destroy himself than admit to the people he loves that he was hurting.

“He’s just so like Dad. He’d rather suffer in silence than talk. He once had a problem with a loan shark to pay off Phainon’s pilot school, and he did not tell any of us. We only knew when he got punched for being one day late,” she huffed into the phone. “Phainon suffered the same trait, sadly. And you! You should talk to him about everything that you meant. Clear things up, if you really care about Phainon. I’ll help set you two up to talk, because Phainon would never ask, and if I say that I could call you for him he’d be like ‘oh no, Mydei is so busy I don’t want to be a bother’ or crap like that. So it’s gotta be you, if you truly want to mend things with him!”

And Mydei wasn’t convinced then, still thinking that Phainon might not like him that way anymore. But then Phainon texted him, saying all the sappy, stupid things, and between all of that vomit of words, he said I love you once.

Once. And it’s already enough to convince him.

So he asked Krateros to arrange a ride to Aedes Elysiae by the end of the night. The old man only raised his brows, looking somewhat amused.

Oh,” he said. “Something urgent there?”

“Phainon,” Mydei answered shortly.

Krateros nodded, like it’s the only reason that ever makes sense. “Is he okay?”

“He is,” Mydei answered again. “We just need to talk.”

“As you should,” Krateros nodded, already pulling up a phone. “Say hello to him for me, yeah? I’m glad you two are okay.”

Mydei paused. “What’s that supposed to mean?”

“You tell me,” Krateros scoffed. “Your brothers in the band had been worried sick about you these past few weeks, and Robin had asked me to talk to you about the whole fake-dating arrangement every chance she got. They thought you would listen to me,” he shook his head. “Bold assumptions. You never listen to anyone but Aglaea and Phainon.”

Mydei rolled his eyes, a little bit surprised that his friends noticed his silence. “No, they’re not.”

“Whatever,” he said. “Come back happier, Mydeimos.”

Mydei had thought how bad he looked for Krateros to even talk like that. But he ignored it and continued going about his day, clinging to the ray of hope he had from Cyrene.

And then, here they are.

When Phainon finally finished his lunch, he asked Mydei to watch movies till we napsies in the living room, saying that he was too tired to go back to the field. Mydei didn’t mind cuddling with Phainon, but imagining Audata,

Hieronymus, or Cyrene walking in on them limb on limb made Mydei feel a little uncomfortable. So he asked to watch the movies in Phainon’s room instead, sharing a small laptop screen that reflected sunlight from the window.

“I’ll buy a big TV later,” Phainon said when the movie started. His voice was already sounding a little bit sleepy. “I’ll put it there, so we can watch movies here more conveniently whenever we’re here.”

Mydei hummed. “This is okay.”

Wrong.

Calling it just okay was an understatement.

This was more than okay.

He had his body half on top of Phainon, his head tucked under Phainon’s left jaw, and he could hear Phainon’s heartbeat from his ear stuck to Phainon’s upper chest.

This was already the most perfect place Mydei had ever been for the past four weeks.

Mydei didn’t even pay attention to the movie anymore, wholly absorbed in Phainon’s presence. The smell of his body mixed with the scent of the sun from the field. His warmth. The rise and fall of his breath, syncing with the harmony of their heartbeats…

Mydei adjusted his head, burying his nose in Phainon’s shoulder, closing his eyes as he mentally chased the dawning melody in his mind while Phainon massaged his scalp idly, his fingers tangled between Mydei’s blond mane.

The melody was soft like Phainon’s bed, warm like his embrace, gentle like Aedes Elysiae’s winds, and flowed like a freshwater stream. It was different from Sons of Gorgo's music, completely tame when compared with his Mother’s beats. This music was just as lovable as Phainon, the sound woven

from the fragments of Phainon’s entire being that Mydei had witnessed and loved.

The harmony that was entirely his.

His feelings. His stories. His heart. His devotion to Phainon and the memories they had woven together, the very ones Mydei held very closely in his heart, the ones he wished to preserve beyond his lifetime. The memories Phainon allowed him to keep echoed through the grand hall of his own mind, singing to him as if it were the only thing that mattered.

The breath of Phainon’s body, the whisper that spoke his mind, the vibration of his soul, the echoes of his stories, the cadence of the familial love he shared with Mydei…

And maybe, maybe the sound of Phainon’s name, too.

Mydei felt almost guilty, as if Phainon were giving him a dime, even though Mydei had taken millions from him. Mydei should take it slowly; he should just listen to the sounds present with him now—just this piece of Phainon in this room, and nothing else.

But that harmony kept playing in his mind, insisting that Mydei breathe life into it, make it an undying melody that could live infinitely in the passage of time.

“You’re humming,”

Phainon’s quiet voice added a ripple to the flow in Mydei’s mind. It didn’t disrupt it; it enriched it like the sound of rain pouring down to the river. “I‘ve never heard of that song. Is it new?”

“Mmhmm,” Mydei hummed. “Mine.”

Phainon didn’t say anything else, knowing exactly what to do, while a fresh wave of inspiration suddenly struck Mydei. Even in the silence, their harmony was so loud. Phainon’s exhale, the sound of his fingers idly playing with the fabric of Mydei’s shirt…

It took quite a while for him to stop, and when he finally quieted down, he could hear Phainon humming along to the melody he had created, which Phainon himself was the inspiration.

“Do that again,” Mydei opened his eyes, tilting his head to meet Phainon’s eyes.

“The humming? Sure.”

Phainon followed Mydei’s lead, humming to the melody that Mydei created. He captured it perfectly, and it made Mydei grin, because Phainon’s melody sounded so lovely in his voice.

“Perfect,” Mydei hummed. “Can I have you record that hum for the song later?”

Phainon blinked, looking surprised. “Um… are you sure?” he said.”I mean, I… okay,” Phainon chuckled. Must be because of looking at Mydei’s narrowed eyes. “Alright, wow, look at me, debuting as a professional hummer.”

“HKS,” Mydei playfully punched Phainon’s belly. Phainon laughed and returned the punch with the same intensity (which wasn’t a lot, honestly. They were too lazy to actually be a threat to each other).

“That doesn’t sound like Sons of Gorgo material,” Phainon commented. “You guys go for a slower ballad this time?”

“No, that song’s not ours,” Mydei said. “Mine.”

Phainon’s fingers that massaged Mydei’s scalp paused. “Um… yours?”

Mydei grabbed Phainon’s other hand, tracing a random pattern on the back of his hand. “After this summer tour,” he said. “The band will take a two-year hiatus.”

“Oh?” Phainon sounded genuinely surprised. “Really, why?”

“Remember when I said Leonnius’s wife is pregnant with twins?” Mydei asked. Phainon hummed an answer, so Mydei continued. “When they went in for the last check before labor, they found out the twins had been hiding a third sibling all along. He had triplets, and Leonnius decided to help take care of them at least until they reached infancy. Perdikkas also said he was thinking about enrolling in med school, and with the two of us gone, we thought maybe it’s time to take a break. Since I graduated high school, we have always gone from tour to tour, studio to studio. We barely have time for ourselves.”

Phainon hummed again, but he didn’t say anything else, seeming content to listen to Mydei.

“So the rest of us decided to look for something to do, too, during the two-year break. Hephaestion got an invitation to be a judge in the School of Rock variety show in Jarilo. That Serval lady had been asking him since the first season. Peucesta and Ptolemy wanted to help compose the music for a Stage Play in Kremnos, while starting their own recording label. It’s a small label under Chrysos Records to help independent musicians rise. Do you wanna know what it’s called?”

“What?” Phainon asked.

“Gorgo Records,” Mydei couldn’t help but feel his own lips curve into a smile. “They said it’s to continue mom’s legacy too. Mom saved em from the street, so they wanna do the same to the kids from Kremnos.”

“That’s so cool. I’m so happy for them.”

Mydei could hear a smile in his words, and it’s so cute that he couldn’t believe that he would let that get away from him. He tightened his hold on Phainon.

“And… what about you?” he asked, brushing a thumb on Mydei’s cheek. “What are you planning to do during the two-year hiatus?”

Mydei shifted their position so they could see each other. Phainon looked gorgeous like this. His skin was a bit darker from the sunburn, but it

somehow made his blue-sky eyes brighter and softer.

“I’m thinking of doing a few solo projects,” he said. “Robin is going to launch a full album next year, a pop-rock album that sounds like Queen Gorgo. The collab's revenue and good PR are finally making the studio confident enough to let her rock. And with her practically carrying Mom’s genre now, I can finally make music for myself. The songs that are truly mine. Not mom’s, not the band’s. Mine.”

Phainon blinked, looking surprised. “I see,” he said. “I’m so happy for you. Have you written the songs yet? How is it going to sound?”

“A little bit of everything. But slow rock, mostly. Alternative. More mellow than the band,” Mydei said. He gazed at Phainon’s eyes, at the smile he had missed so, so much. “It’s mostly love songs with slower beats, maybe a few folk-rock experiments here and there.”

“Folk-rock? That sounds so cool. I’ve never heard anything like that before!” Phainon said excitedly. “I’m sure you could pull it off nicely. Mydeimos Gorgo isn’t just some rockstar’s son. He is the rockstar!”

Mydei chuckled. “Give me your guitar and I can sing it for you now.”

“Hm?” Phainon blinked. There was this unmistakable excitement flickering in his eyes; the ones he always seemed to have whenever he heard Mydei was doing something even slightly interesting. He shifted to pause the movie, dedicating his attention entirely to Mydei. “That sounds appealing. But can’t you do it a cappella instead? I kinda don’t wanna move. It’s super cozy here.”

“Mm,” Mydei hummed, snuggled closer to Phainon in agreement. “Alright, then.”

And so, he started singing the songs he had been writing for the past few weeks. The genuine feeling he had been keeping to himself, the song about their time in Aedes Elysiae, their lovely weekends full of touches, kisses, and desire, a song that was dedicated to Phainon’s sky blue eyes, and Worldbearer, a song where Mydei admitted openly through the lyrics how

Phainon had been carrying Mydei’s world singlehandedly, giving him a countryside family to live in, a taste of domesticity, and a love so silly, so gentle, and full of fire that it ignited something warm inside him. Something he didn’t know existed outside of the romance movie.

Something he didn’t know existed in real life.

He originally wrote those songs as ballads. An album of bittersweet memories he thought he had lost and could never get back. But now that he literally lived inside those lyrics, he mixed them up with the melody he had only discovered now, the melody he had woven into Phainon’s name.

And the muse himself—Phainon, was listening quietly, as if his life depended on it.

… And all my life, I’ve only lived through the motions, A grave-writ script recited like a premonition. But the sun in your eyes breaks through my static world, Your light, warm enough to thaw the cold.

Your hands on mine My shattered skies are gone. Your smile—it shines, Burn bright like a dawn And there might be someone braver, kinder, prettier, but no one carries me better than you, my worldbearer.

“... and da-da-da, I hadn’t written the rest of the lyrics for the last one,” Mydei said, ending the last part with a snicker. “Most of it only struck me just now, so that’s all I have, but…”

Phainon cupped Mydei’s cheeks, looking positively beaming. “‘Dei, it’s beautiful,” he whispered. “That song is so, so beautiful.”

Mydei grinned, another wave of warmth bloomed in his chest. The one only Phainon could create. “You’ve made a great muse.”

“Oh?” Phainon chuckled. “Is it written for me? Why, Mydeimos. I feel so loved right now.”

Mydei smiled. “Well, you better, HKS,” he said. “'Cause I really do love you.”

Phainon let out the tiniest laugh, brushing his thumb on Mydei’s lower lip. “Say it again.”

“I love you,” Mydei said, louder this time. He inched closer, placing a tiny peck on Phainon’s lips and the tip of his nose.

“Hear that, world?” Phainon suddenly spoke loudly. “Mydeimos loves me!”

A muffled Shut Up! was heard from Cyrene’s room, and Phainon blinked, startled with the unexpected response. Mydei laughed, poking at Phainon’s nose and calling him a dork.

“You know what, I love you too,” Phainon said. “And I will make sure you know, I will love you forever from here on. No more hiding something.”

“Not even if it’s for my own good?” Mydei challenged.

“No,” Phainon said. “I will tell you everything.”

“Me too,” Mydei hummed. He would rather NOT have the last four hellish weeks again. Heck, he didn’t even want to remember it ever happened.

It felt so claustrophobic, holding the hand of a woman he considered a younger sister and trying to make it look romantic while under the gaze of so many eyes and cameras. The fame that had been following him since childhood now magnified, cornered him everywhere, even in the safety of

his own house. It was exhausting to spare a few hours of his day to read all the pre-submitted questions from the interviewees, consider what to answer, how the public would react, and rehearse his gestures and expressions for each interview so that Phainon wouldn’t misinterpret them. It was exhausting to have to come to Aventurine and fight his way to tamper with the plan.

“What, you haven’t told him?” Aventurine chuckled.

Oh, this bastard.

“Because it’s not even final, yet” Mydei scoffed. “But fine, so remember when I said I’m planning to have solo projects?” he turned to Phainon, who only nodded. “Yeah, I don’t plan to go on tour as intensely as Sons of Gorgo in this project, so I uh… I may have mentioned that I will be considering Aventurine’s offer as a Celebrity Judge for MegaChef,” Mydei said, glaring at Aventurine when he emphasized the word considering.

At that, Phainon’s brows shot up so high they almost disappeared behind his bangs.

“Oh,” he said. “So… so you’ll be home more often?”

Mydei almost laughed. Of course, that’s what Phainon paid attention to. He was just so adorable. He looked almost like Big Snowy now, and Mydei could even imagine him wagging his tail, if he ever had any.

“Maybe? Yeah, kinda,” Mydei shifted on his feet, suddenly feeling nervous with the whole implication of him being the house hus… house partner. “It’s still under discussion, though, right, Aventurine?”

“Aw, come on, you’re thrilled, and you know it,” Aventurine clapped, bracelets jangling. “Between that and The Noise, you’ll skyrocket IPC’s

ratings. Millions rolling in, guaranteed. Veritas already ran the numbers— trust me, they’re pretty.” He leaned forward, patting the box with a sly grin. “Which is why I bringing a gift. Especially for Captain Khaslana.”

“Oh,” Robin shifted her eyes from Phainon’s left hand, now decorated with pretty pressed-on nails. “Is this the gift that you’ve discussed with my brother, Mister Aventurine?”

“The very one,” Aventurine smirked smugly. “Have you done with the nails, baby bird? I want Captain Khaslana to be the one to unwrap this gift. After all, it was because of him we’re all here counting our successes and well, gains, if you know what I mean.”

“Juuust a little bit more,” Robin said. She pressed a nail on top of Phainon’s ring finger, decorated with a gold and red motif, and raised her hand. “Yup, all done!”

“So, captain,” Aventurine urged, the corners of his mouth tugging higher. “If you would.”

Phainon hesitated, glancing between Mydei and the box like it might explode.

Robin clasped her hands together, bouncing with excitement. “Open it, Captain!”

So, he did. Carefully, he peeled back the glossy wrapping and lifted the lid. Inside, nestled in layers of velvet, sat a gleaming scale model of a mini jet. Complete with the tail number and the manufacturer’s crest. Under that, there’s a flight logbook, its leather cover embossed with the golden crest of a falcon.

Mydei raised his brows. He glanced at Aventurine, who was grinning in a way that looked like he had just won a game against Mydei.

Which he did. As much as Mydei hated to admit it, Aventurine kind of beat Mydei into buying Phainon his own jet.

Mydei sneered. Oh, he was so going to get back at Aventurine for this.

“Um, this is nice,” Phainon said. “I don’t know much about Bombardier planes, but it’s cute. And the logbook…” he paused, and Mydei could almost see his gears grinding, and how all the physical evidence clicked in Phainon’s mind before he shot his eyes up to Aventurine. “This belongs to a real jet.”

“Yup.”

“With my name.”

“A super rock and roll gift!” Robin chuckled.

“Yes, not officiated yet since I still need your ID, and whatever for your paperwork but—”

“Aventurine,” Phainon said sternly, like he was forcing Aventurine to be serious. “This is an actual Bombardier plane. This costs double-digit millions of credits.”

“Very true, I see you’re very knowledgeable in the jet department,” Aventurine cackled. “Don’t worry about the numbers, Captain. Have you seen the earnings reports for the Mydei-Robin fake-dating campaign? I only make a little percentage of that profit, and yet, this plane only costs me a little of what I make,” he flashed a grin. “Consider it a compensation for your trouble. Or maybe a friendship offering from me. You know, I like to keep my friends happy,” he added with a wink.

Mydei could see Ratio roll his eyes. “If you’ve actually seen that number, getting you a 6000 model is kind of a stingy gift. Especially considering what I heard happened in your relationship,” Ratio crossed his arms. “I say you could demand a 7500 model instead with…”

“Ah ah ah, honey, please, don’t spoil our pillow talk to our friends,” Aventurine interrupted him, letting his usual smirk spark with a little bit of fake shyness. Mydei knew that it wasn’t the case. It was just their dynamic; Ratio countering him, and Aventurine deflected him just to be annoying. He

almost jabbed at Aventurine, if only he weren’t so distracted by Phainon’s face, looking at the plane model as if it horrified him.

Mydei shook his head, feeling a little bit regretful for not thinking about buying an actual private jet for Phainon sooner. Though it was not without reason. He always believed that Phainon was a little bit too difficult to give expensive gifts. Phainon still insisted on paying for the groceries, and when they moved into that apartment, Phainon’s concern about the rate of the space was so palpable that Mydei asked Krateros to handle the house buying, so he wouldn’t know the actual price and taxes to Phainon, and thus, never had to mention it.

But maybe he didn’t try to make him understand enough.

Mydei sighed, begrudgingly accepting his defeat to Aventurine this time.

Phainon’s lips parted, no sound coming out at first. He looked like a boy again, wide-eyed, holding the little model as if it were a burning coal.

“But…” he paused, gaping like a fish. “Mydei?”

Mydei shrugged. “Ratio was right, you were supposed to get a better model,” he said. “You’ve put up with his craziness. And considering the profit Aventurine said we make…”

“Next time, talk to me about your discomfort, and I do not have to think about compensation at all,” Aventurine remarked.

“But you should have thought about it, if you ever care about anyone’s feelings,” Ratio scolded.

“Fine, whatever, I have to do everything around here, huh? By Qlipoth, do you guys want me to mop the floor too?” Aventurine rolled his eyes dramatically, but not without a grin on his lips.

Robin chuckled, as if knowing that it was just Aventurine’s usual antics. Maybe it was. As much as Mydei didn’t like him, he had to admit that even though he’s a scheming bastard, Aventurine was actually playing his cards

fairly. A private jet as a gift was not something to take lightly. It costs a fortune, even considering Aventurine’s net worth. Mydei could respect him for the good intention alone.

“But guys?” Phainon asked again. “Do you… have any idea how much it costs to maintain one of these? The hangar fees, the insurance, the— Kephale almighty, the fuel alone would bleed us dry in a month! Mydei. I…”

At that, Aventurine’s smile faltered. “Wait…” he said. “Mydei, did you not tell him how much you make a month?”

Oh shit.

“He never asked,” Mydei said defensively. “He knew the pin to my bank account. Phainon, you should have known.”

“I’m not peeking at your bank account. I’m not that kind of guy,” Phainon scrunched his nose, as the idea itself disgusted him. “I could still pay for the groceries just fine, including that Kobe Beef you like to buy every now and then.”

Aventurine raised his brows, looking absolutely entertained, now. “Wh… you pay for the groceries?” he chuckled. “Mydei, really?”

“What about it?” Phainon said, looking defensive all of a sudden. “He bought the house. I gotta help maintain it, right?”

“Oh dear Qlipoth,” Aventurine cackled now, shoulders shaking with laughter. “No wonder Mydei went all the way for you. All of those hassles Mydei caused me to make a lot of sense, now. No wonder he’s so attached to you,” he shook his head. “You know, Phainon, if my boyfriend is one of the biggest rock stars in the world, I would just let him bankroll everything and just enjoy my life completely spoiled rotten. He’s not just a rockstar. He is The Rockstar, you know that, right?”

“Mister Aventurine!” Robin shook her head. “Don’t punish Phainon for being a complete gentleman!”

“Took words right out of my mouth,” Ratio added. “Also, speak for yourself. You don’t even let me bankroll everything and insist on working your ass off.”

“It’s cause the IPC would go bankrupt without me, and I like to spoil you, honey,” Aventurine winked at Ratio. “But alright, fine, Mister Gentleman. If it makes you feel better, I’ll help with the hangar fee for the first year and…”

“Nonsense,” Mydei cut off, feeling a bit disturbed that him allowing Phainon to provide for him, becoming the subject of Aventurine’s jab. “Don’t worry about the maintenance and stuff. Just focus on flying it, okay? Fly me when you have the time.”

Robin cooed and clapped like it was the best song she’d ever heard. Aventurine raised a toast with an invisible glass. Ratio sighed, long-suffering, like he’d already foreseen this exact chaos.

Phainon opened his mouth, closed it again, and opened it again. He looked like he still had a lot to say, but upon seeing the plane model, Mydei, and Robin, his gaze softened, and Mydei could almost sense it.

“I guess, alright, thanks,” he said, shifting his eyes to Mydei again. “It could take me months to get the type-rating, but… I don’t mind flying my rockstar boyfriend and going with him on tour every once in a while.”

“Perfect,” Aventurine smiled. “Now, would you listen to my top-of-mind idea on how the Mydei-Robin breakup campaign would roll? Spoiler alert: The angst is expected to gain us another million. Do you know how long sad songs usually last? And how much do they usually sell?”

Mydei rolled his eyes and hmph-ed loudly so Aventurine could hear him. They still had months to go on the Cherry Bomb fake relationship idea, but here Aventurine was, already set with a timeline for moving on to the next one.

But he didn’t mind. Because this time, he would make sure none of them messed up.

This time, it wouldn’t cost him his real relationship again.

-

A few more weeks have blurred past since then. The ruse was still in motion; the tour was as hectic as it could be, and yet their relationship had only gotten stronger.

Phainon would tell Mydei when he saw something on social media he didn’t like. Mydei would assure him with his confession of love. Sometimes he made it so cringe that Phainon would laugh and later apologize. Phainon helped rehearse Mydei’s answers for the interview whenever he got a chance. When he wasn’t, Mydei would text him all about it. When he couldn’t text Phainon, Mydei would ask Krateros to do that in his stead, or Hephaestion, or Robin, if she had the time.

Though Phainon immediately asked him to skip Hephaestion. That man, apparently, did not shy away from using that opportunity to send an embarrassing text that none of them would ever want to read twice.

But Mydei still couldn’t forget Phainon’s face when Robin finally exchanged her number with him. He looked at his phone for one full minute, and then, slowly looking at Mydei and said, “I think the ten-year-old Phainon is screaming in joy somewhere inside my brain.”

And Mydei had only laughed.

It amazed him—how, even with Mydei tangled in tour rehearsals and solo project preparations, and Phainon buried under his flight schedules and their new jet’s Type Rating test—they still carved out time for each other through phone calls, video chats, voice notes, and random pictures. Maybe they should’ve been honest from the outset, with themselves and with those closest to them.

Now, with a week off before the second leg of the world tour and Aglaea having allowed the band a week's rest, Mydei decided to come home. By fortune, Phainon told him that he would be home by the weekend as well. He had just completed his ultra-long-haul journey and was on mandatory rest.

For the first time in weeks, they finally had real time together.

And boy, did Phainon waste no time.

The moment Mydei stepped into the room, Phainon quickly grabbed him, pushed him back into their bed, and kissed him like a starving man. There was no preamble—just raw urgency, the kind that made Mydei’s chest squeeze with longing and desire.

Mydei couldn’t possibly stay still in the face of that kind of passion. He kissed back, just as hungry, just as greedy, their lips clashing like a dare with each other. They wrestled for dominance—hands tugging, pulling, stripping clothes away piece by piece—until the bed became too small for the war they waged.

Too late, Mydei realized they had rolled to the edge.

Phainon toppled to the carpet with a muted thud, dragging Mydei with him.

Mydei broke the kiss to ask if Phainon was alright, if he was hurt. Phainon only chuckled, soft and breathy, already chasing his lips again. He rolled them back onto the floor with reckless abandon, his darkened eyes glinting with challenge and a tease.

Oh.

Oh, it’s on.

He kissed Phainon twice as eagerly, their giggles and longing tangling with groans as they rolled across the carpet. He didn’t even know where they were in the room anymore, until Phainon’s hand suddenly cupped the back of his head, protecting him from the sharp corner of the bedside table.

“Careful,” Phainon teased between ragged breaths, laughter tumbling with the words. “Watch where you move, Kotik.”

“Mmm, can’t,” Mydei murmured, already peppering kisses across Phainon’s skin that he could reach. “I’ve got a battle to win.”

Phainon caught his lips in a quick peck, then another, then another, speaking between them as though each syllable was a kiss itself: “Mm, love, me, my, kitten, with, concussion.”

Mydei laughed. “Silly dog.”

“Woof woof,” Phainon answered, brushing a thumb on Mydei’s kiss-swollen lips. Mydei leaned to kiss him again, but Phainon kept him in place. “Wait.”

Mydei arched a brow. “What, truce already?”

“As if,” Phainon smirked. “I’ve got something in my pants to show you, before you actually take them off.”

Mydei snorted, leaning closer as he teasingly pressed his hips against Phainon’s. “I’ve seen everything in your pants. And I love it better when it’s unwrapped properly.”

Phainon’s breathy laughter was mixed with a hint of nervousness. “Kinky,” he said. “But I’m serious, ‘Dei. Just a moment.”

Mydei blinked, tilting his head. “Alright,” he said. “Shoot, then.”

Phainon shifted, rolling onto his side. His hand dipped into the pocket of his lounge pants, fishing for something. Mydei’s brow raised, half expecting another joke or, Kephale forbids, something even kinkier. There was no telling with Phainon.

But to his surprise, Phainon pulled out a slim velvet box and opened it to reveal a matching pair of rings with a special shape and carving, one in Mydei’s red and one in Phainon’s eye color. They sparkled under the light of their room.

Mydei could feel his heart skip a beat.

“You know, it’s… It’s not exactly a proposal. Kinda… but, we don’t have to make it that way if you’re not comfortable with it?” Phainon’s voice was hushed now, uncertain in a way that twisted Mydei’s chest. It was kind of weird for him to look so boyish when his eyes were still dark from the desire they shared a second ago.

“It’s just… um… something like a promise ring? I don’t know, I don’t want to push you into something serious too soon, but I wanted something that marked us. Something real,” He shrugged, laughing weakly, like he was trying to make light of his own stumbling and trembling. “I mean, I only kind of want something in your color that I could wear, and when I ask Cartonus, I thought, why not make one for you, too? I… uh… you know,” he laughed, helpless, as if afraid to look up.

Mydei did not respond.

Instead, he got to his feet, leaving Phainon on the floor while he walked to the other side of the wardrobe. He grabbed something in the furthest corner of the drawer, the one he had been thinking about since that day in Aedes Elysiae.

“Mydei?” Phainon asked, confused and unsure.

Mydei sat before Phainon again, who was looking at him nervously, and his velvet box was still out in the open. Mydei showed the ring that he grabbed, the one that his mother gave him when he was very young, when that ring was too large even for his thumb.

“Marry me, Phainon Khaslana of Aedes Elysiae,” he whispered, the words leaped out of Mydei before he even knew he was saying them. His pulse raced; his own voice had cut him off. Phainon’s eyes went wide, the box still trembling between his fingers.

“…M… Mydei?”

“Marry me.” Mydei’s throat tightened, but he said it again, firmer, like an order and a plea tangled together. “I don’t care if it’s stupid, I don’t care if it’s too soon, I don’t care if half the world thinks we’re insane. You bring me a matching ring and tell me it’s not a proposal?” He laughed, his heart raced like a formula car and he could even sense his own giddiness, it’s almost embarrassing. “You’re a fucking coward, Phainon Khaslana.”

Phainon’s lips parted, and for a moment all Mydei could see was disbelief flashing into something brighter—something softer. His laughter came out choked, wet at the edges, and he shook his head like he couldn’t believe it.

“Shut up,” he said. “It was a proposal. I was just worried that I’m pushing it, and you think it’s too soon, and we could always talk it over…”

“Yeah, you shut up,” Mydei said, grabbing Phainon’s hand and slipping the ring on his finger. “And do your thing, Fos mou. Make me a Khaslana, too.”

“You’re taking my na—yeah, yep, okay, Kotik,” Phainon let out a nervous exhale. He pulled the ring from the box, placing the one with the blue gem to Mydei’s ring finger. “Okay, Mydeimos Khaslana.”

Mydei grabbed the other ring from the box and slipped it onto Phainon’s finger, gazing at how beautiful it looked above his mother’s old band—the ring Gorgo had once given Eurypon, and later reclaimed when that love fell apart. He kissed the ring, promising himself that he—no, they—would carry this one into a better love story: the happy ending his mother had always dreamed of.

He would fight for Phainon again and again, in this lifetime and the next. He would love Phainon the way he deserved to be loved.

And as Phainon kissed his ring too, then Mydei’s knuckles one by one, Mydei knew he felt the same.

After all, Phainon had always helped him carry his mother’s love and legacy—gladly, as if it were his own.
